description: Final Tier 1–7 exercise vocabulary and definitions for the current Rep Wars exercise library. Tier 1 intentionally remains broad; Tier 8 does not add new exercise vocabulary.

1.description: Foundational movement library. Exercises are introduced progressively across 1A, 1B, and 1C. Advancing to a new band adds exercises to the player's permanent library and does not remove previously unlocked exercises.

2.description: Tier 2 expands the permanent exercise library beyond Tier 1. Every Tier 1 exercise remains available. New exercises are introduced only when they represent a meaningful increase in movement capability, coordination, leverage, balance, or control. Rep and duration prescriptions are intentionally not defined here.

3.description: Tier 3 expands the permanent exercise library beyond Tier 2. All previously unlocked exercises remain permanently available. New Tier 3 movements introduce meaningful increases in leverage, unilateral demand, balance, multiplanar control, trunk complexity, coordination, or carefully introduced explosive movement. Rep and duration prescriptions are intentionally excluded.

4.description: Tier 4 expands the permanent exercise library beyond Tier 3. All previously unlocked exercises remain permanently available. New exercises introduce meaningful increases in unilateral strength, leverage, balance, coordination, trunk control, locomotion complexity, and selected explosive movement. No exercise is included merely because it looks harder; each addition must provide a distinct capability or a necessary progression step. Rep and duration prescriptions are intentionally excluded.

5.description: Tier 5 expands the permanent exercise library beyond Tier 4. All previously unlocked exercises remain permanently available. New exercises emphasize advanced bodyweight leverage, unilateral control, posterior-chain strength, balance, trunk control, and progressively more demanding elastic and explosive movement. Rep and duration prescriptions are intentionally excluded.

6.description: Tier 6 expands the permanent exercise library beyond Tier 5. All previously unlocked exercises remain permanently available. New exercises introduce substantially advanced leverage, unilateral strength, balance, trunk control, elastic movement, and selected higher-skill bodyweight capabilities. Rep and duration prescriptions are intentionally excluded.

7.description: Tier 7 completes the current exercise vocabulary with advanced bodyweight skill and strength capabilities. All previously unlocked exercises remain permanently available, and no new exercise vocabulary is introduced in Tier 8.

BAND_1A.label: Foundational Movement
BAND_1A.description: Stable, supported, low-complexity introductory movement patterns.

BAND_1B.label: Foundational Independent Movement
BAND_1B.description: Reduced support and increased coordination while retaining broadly accessible movement patterns.

BAND_1C.label: Foundational Strength and Control
BAND_1C.description: More independent movement, greater control demands, and stronger expression of foundational patterns.

BAND_2A.label: Foundational Strength
BAND_2A.description: Introduces the first clearly independent strength and coordination challenges beyond Tier 1 while retaining relatively stable movement environments.

BAND_2B.label: Developing Strength and Control
BAND_2B.description: Builds on Tier 2A with greater leverage, unilateral demand, coordination, or sustained control.

BAND_2C.label: Advanced Foundation
BAND_2C.description: Completes the Tier 2 foundation with more demanding bodyweight variations and coordinated movement while avoiding premature advanced-skill or high-impact exercises.

BAND_3A.label: Developing Complexity
BAND_3A.description: Introduces more demanding unilateral, multiplanar, lever-based, and coordinated movements while retaining controlled execution.

BAND_3B.label: Developing Advanced Control
BAND_3B.description: Builds on 3A with greater balance, coordination, unilateral loading, trunk demands, and selected dynamic movement.

BAND_3C.label: Advanced Foundational Control
BAND_3C.description: Completes Tier 3 with substantially more demanding bodyweight control and coordination while reserving the highest-skill variations for later tiers.

BAND_4A.label: Advanced Strength and Coordination
BAND_4A.description: Introduces more demanding unilateral strength, leverage, coordination, and dynamic control while maintaining manageable movement complexity.

BAND_4B.label: Advanced Dynamic Control
BAND_4B.description: Builds on 4A with more substantial single-leg strength, dynamic balance, locomotion, and selected explosive movement.

BAND_4C.label: Advanced Bodyweight Skill
BAND_4C.description: Completes Tier 4 with higher-skill bodyweight movements and more demanding coordination, while reserving the most extreme strength and impact challenges for later tiers.

BAND_5A.label: Advanced Strength
BAND_5A.description: Introduces substantially harder bodyweight strength and control tasks while retaining clear movement patterns.

BAND_5B.label: Advanced Coordination
BAND_5B.description: Builds on 5A with greater leverage, unilateral control, elastic movement, and multi-part coordination.

BAND_5C.label: Advanced Bodyweight Capability
BAND_5C.description: Completes Tier 5 with demanding unilateral, balance, leverage, and explosive capabilities while reserving the most extreme skills for later tiers.

BAND_6A.label: High-Level Strength and Control
BAND_6A.description: Introduces advanced leverage and unilateral control while remaining focused on deliberate, controlled bodyweight movement.

BAND_6B.label: High-Level Dynamic Capability
BAND_6B.description: Builds on 6A with more difficult unilateral propulsion, elastic movement, trunk control, and coordinated strength.

BAND_6C.label: Advanced Bodyweight Mastery
BAND_6C.description: Completes Tier 6 with high-demand bodyweight skills while reserving the most extreme strength and technical movements for later tiers.

BAND_7A.label: Advanced Skill Foundation
BAND_7A.description: Introduces major advanced bodyweight skills that require substantial prior strength, control, balance, or compression capacity.

BAND_7B.label: Advanced Strength Skill
BAND_7B.description: Builds on 7A with demanding dynamic strength skills, longer leverage, and more advanced control requirements.

BAND_7C.label: Elite Bodyweight Skill
BAND_7C.description: Completes Tier 7 with the most demanding current cataloged bodyweight skills, including advanced leverage, unilateral strength, pulling, and skill control.

KNEE_EXTENSION_QUADRICEPS.description: Knee-extension movements emphasizing controlled quadriceps strength through the knee.

TRUNK_LATERAL_FLEXION.description: Exercises whose primary trunk action is controlled lateral flexion or side-bending.

POSTERIOR_CHAIN_KNEE_FLEXION.description: Exercises whose primary progression is controlled hamstring-driven knee flexion rather than hip-dominant hinging.

TRUNK_COMPRESSION.description: Exercises centered on maintaining or producing a compressed trunk-and-hip position, often with substantial hip-flexor involvement and/or shoulder support.

VERTICAL_PULL.description: Bodyweight pulling movements in which the primary progression is vertical pulling strength, scapular control, and increasingly unilateral loading.

TRUNK_ANTI_ROTATION.description: Exercises that challenge the trunk to resist unwanted rotational movement while the limbs move or load shifts.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up
exercises.description: A supported horizontal push performed while standing angled toward a wall.
setup: Stand facing a clear wall.
Place your hands on the wall at about chest height.
Step back enough to create a comfortable body angle.
steps: Bend your elbows to bring your body toward the wall.
Keep your body aligned as you approach the wall.
Press through your hands to return to the starting position.
keyCues: Keep your body in one controlled line.
Keep the hands stable on the wall.
completionCriteria: A controlled lowering phase is completed.
The player presses back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Sit-to-Stand
exercises.description: A supported squat pattern in which the player lowers to a seat and returns to standing.
setup: Place a sturdy chair or similar stable surface behind you.
Stand with your feet in a comfortable stance.
Position yourself so the seat is available for controlled contact.
steps: Bend your knees and hips to lower toward the seat.
Touch the seat under control without collapsing onto it.
Press through your feet to return to standing.
keyCues: Use the seat as a guide, not a drop.
completionCriteria: The player makes controlled contact with the seat.
The player returns fully to standing.

exercises.name: Wall Hip Hinge
exercises.description: A foundational hip-hinge drill using a wall as a positional target.
setup: Stand with your back toward a wall.
Place your feet far enough forward that your hips can move toward the wall.
Keep your stance comfortable.
steps: Soften your knees slightly.
Push your hips backward toward the wall while keeping the trunk controlled.
Drive through your feet and return to standing.
keyCues: Move the hips back rather than squatting down.
Use the wall as a target.
completionCriteria: The hips move back to the wall or near the wall under control.
The player returns to upright standing.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A supported hip-extension movement performed lying on the back.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Place your feet flat on the floor.
Rest your arms comfortably at your sides.
steps: Press through your feet to lift your hips.
Reach the top of the bridge with control.
Lower your hips back to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The hips clearly lift from the floor.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Supported Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: A supported reverse-lunge pattern using external support for balance.
setup: Stand beside a stable support.
Hold the support lightly as needed.
Begin standing tall with feet under you.
steps: Step one foot backward.
Lower until the front leg is comfortably loaded while maintaining balance.
Drive through the front foot to return to standing.
keyCues: Use support for balance rather than pulling yourself upward.
completionCriteria: A controlled step-back and lowering phase is completed.
The player returns to the starting stance.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.description: A bilateral calf raise performed from a stable standing position.
setup: Stand near a stable support if needed.
Place both feet comfortably on the floor.
Stand upright.
steps: Rise onto the balls of both feet.
Reach a controlled top position.
Lower the heels back down.
keyCues: Use support only as needed for balance.
completionCriteria: The heels lift from the floor.
The heels return under control.

exercises.name: Tiptoe Walk
exercises.description: A low-speed walking pattern performed on the balls of the feet.
setup: Stand upright with space to walk safely.
Rise onto the balls of both feet.
steps: Take small controlled steps forward while staying on the balls of the feet.
Continue the walking pattern with steady balance.
Return to normal standing when finished.
completionCriteria: The prescribed continuous walking interval is completed while maintaining the tiptoe position.

exercises.name: Supported Single-Leg Balance
exercises.description: A supported single-leg balance exercise using a stable external support.
setup: Stand beside a stable support.
Place one hand lightly on the support.
Stand tall with both feet under you.
steps: Shift your weight onto one leg.
Lift the other foot clear of the floor.
Maintain the supported single-leg position.
Return the lifted foot to the floor under control.
keyCues: Use only as much hand support as needed.
Keep the standing knee comfortably unlocked.
completionCriteria: One foot remains off the floor for the prescribed hold duration.
The player returns to a stable two-foot stance.

exercises.name: Supine March
exercises.description: A supine trunk-stability movement using controlled alternating leg lifts.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Position your arms comfortably beside you.
steps: Brace gently through the trunk.
Lift one foot while keeping the pelvis stable.
Return it to the floor and alternate sides.
keyCues: Move one leg at a time.
completionCriteria: Each alternating leg lift and return is completed with the trunk remaining controlled.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Dead Bug
exercises.description: A shortened-lever dead-bug variation emphasizing controlled trunk stability.
setup: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent.
Raise the legs to a comfortable bent position.
Reach the arms upward.
steps: Lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return both limbs to the start.
Repeat on the opposite side.
keyCues: Keep the lower back and pelvis controlled.
Move slowly enough to maintain position.
completionCriteria: The opposite arm and leg lower and return without losing trunk control.

exercises.name: Knee Plank
exercises.description: A shortened-lever plank performed from the knees.
setup: Place your hands or forearms on the floor as appropriate.
Place your knees on the floor behind your hips.
Align the trunk in a straight supported position.
steps: Brace your trunk.
Maintain the plank position for the prescribed duration.
Lower back to the floor when finished.
keyCues: Do not let the hips sag or lift excessively.
completionCriteria: The supported plank position is established.
The prescribed hold duration is completed without losing the position.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.placementRationale: Develops trunk anti-rotation and control while opposite limbs move independently.
exercises.description: A quadruped anti-rotation exercise using controlled opposite-limb extension.
setup: Start on hands and knees.
Place hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
steps: Brace the trunk.
Extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Return both limbs under control.
Repeat on the opposite side.
keyCues: Move slowly enough to stay balanced.
completionCriteria: The opposite arm and leg extend and return without a major trunk shift.

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.description: A basic controlled trunk-flexion exercise performed lying on the back.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Place your hands lightly behind or beside your head.
steps: Curl your upper trunk upward a small controlled amount.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower back to the starting position.
keyCues: Lift through the trunk rather than pulling the head.
completionCriteria: The upper trunk lifts from the floor.
The player returns under control.

exercises.name: Heel Tap
exercises.description: A low-range alternating trunk-flexion movement performed from a bent-knee supine position.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Place your arms alongside your body.
steps: Lift the head and shoulders slightly.
Reach one hand toward the same-side heel.
Return to center and repeat on the other side.
completionCriteria: Each side reaches toward the heel and returns under control.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Dead Bug
exercises.placementRationale: Uses contralateral limb movement to challenge the trunk to resist unwanted rotation while maintaining position.
exercises.description: A dead-bug variation combining opposite-arm and leg movement while resisting trunk rotation.
setup: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent.
Raise the arms toward the ceiling.
steps: Brace the trunk.
Lower one arm and the opposite leg in a controlled pattern.
Return to the starting position.
Alternate sides.
keyCues: Use only the range you can control.
completionCriteria: The opposite arm and leg complete a controlled lower-and-return cycle without a major trunk shift.

exercises.name: March
exercises.description: A controlled alternating marching movement performed from standing.
setup: Stand upright with clear space around you.
Let the arms rest naturally or swing comfortably.
steps: Lift one knee in a controlled step.
Lower the foot and alternate to the other side.
Continue the alternating pattern.
completionCriteria: The alternating march continues for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Alternating Toe Tap
exercises.description: An alternating standing toe-tap pattern emphasizing controlled weight shifting.
setup: Stand upright with clear floor space.
Keep one foot planted while preparing the other to move.
steps: Tap one foot lightly forward or to the designated target.
Return it to the starting position.
Alternate sides continuously.
completionCriteria: The alternating toe-tap pattern continues for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Lateral Step
exercises.description: A controlled side-stepping pattern performed continuously.
setup: Stand upright with space to move laterally.
Face forward.
steps: Step one foot to the side.
Bring the other foot toward it without crossing.
Continue stepping side to side.
completionCriteria: The prescribed continuous lateral-stepping interval is completed.

exercises.name: Step-Back
exercises.description: A controlled alternating backward step pattern.
setup: Stand upright with clear space behind you.
Keep your torso facing forward.
steps: Step one foot backward.
Bring it forward to the starting stance.
Alternate to the other side.
completionCriteria: The alternating step-back pattern continues for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.description: A gentle quadruped mobility sequence alternating spinal flexion and extension.
setup: Start on hands and knees.
Place hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
steps: Round the spine comfortably while allowing the head to follow.
Then move toward a gentle extended position without forcing the range.
Alternate smoothly.
keyCues: Do not force the end positions.
completionCriteria: A controlled flexion-and-extension cycle is completed.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: A supported half-kneeling stretch emphasizing the hip-flexor side of the rear leg.
setup: Kneel with one knee down and the other foot forward.
Keep the torso upright.
Position the front foot far enough forward to feel stable.
steps: Gently shift the hips forward while keeping the pelvis controlled.
Stop at a comfortable stretch.
Return to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The stretch position is established and held for the prescribed duration before returning.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: A controlled hamstring stretch performed from a stable standing or supported position.
setup: Stand or sit in a stable position appropriate to the variation.
Extend one leg comfortably.
steps: Hinge or lean toward the extended leg until a gentle stretch is felt.
Hold the position without bouncing.
Return under control.
completionCriteria: A gentle stretch position is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Quad Stretch
exercises.description: A standing or side-lying quadriceps stretch using controlled positioning.
setup: Stand near a stable support if needed.
Bend one knee and bring the heel toward the body.
steps: Hold the foot or ankle comfortably.
Keep the knees relatively close as tolerated.
Maintain the stretch without forcing it.
keyCues: Keep the knee in a comfortable position.
completionCriteria: A comfortable quadriceps stretch is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch
exercises.description: A supported calf stretch using a split stance and controlled forward weight shift.
setup: Place one foot behind the other with the rear heel down.
Face a wall or other stable support.
Use the support for balance.
steps: Bend the front knee slightly and shift forward.
Keep the rear heel grounded.
Hold the gentle stretch.
completionCriteria: A gentle calf stretch is held for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.description: A kneeling rest position with the hips moving toward the heels and the arms reaching forward.
setup: Start on hands and knees.
Bring your hips toward your heels as comfortable.
Reach the arms forward or rest them beside you.
steps: Settle into the position gradually.
Keep breathing comfortably.
Return to the starting position when finished.
keyCues: Do not force the hips or knees.
completionCriteria: The supported position is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Adductor Rock-Back
exercises.description: A quadruped mobility drill that gently moves the hips backward with one leg extended to the side.
setup: Start on hands and knees.
Extend one leg out to the side with the foot supported.
steps: Shift the hips backward toward the planted leg.
Return forward to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side as prescribed.
completionCriteria: A controlled backward-and-forward cycle is completed without forcing the end range.

exercises.name: Heel Slide
exercises.description: A supine hamstring knee-flexion drill using a sliding heel to control the bend-and-extend action.
setup: Lie on your back with one or both legs extended comfortably.
Place the heel on a surface that allows it to slide.
steps: Bend the knee by drawing the heel toward the body.
Pause briefly at the comfortable end of the range.
Slide the heel back to the starting position.
keyCues: Move from the knee and hamstring.
completionCriteria: The heel slides in and returns through a controlled range.

exercises.name: Ankle Rock
exercises.description: A standing or half-kneeling ankle mobility drill using controlled forward movement of the knee.
setup: Place one foot flat on the floor with the heel grounded.
Position the body so the knee can move forward over the foot.
steps: Gently drive the knee forward over the foot.
Return to the starting position.
Repeat smoothly.
keyCues: Move only through a comfortable range.
Track the knee in line with the foot.
completionCriteria: The knee moves forward and returns without the heel lifting.

exercises.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Expands the permanent non-progression mobility library.
exercises.description: A doorway-supported chest stretch using a comfortable arm position.
setup: Stand in a doorway.
Place the forearm or hand against the frame in a comfortable position.
Step the body forward slightly.
steps: Shift gently forward until a stretch is felt across the chest and front shoulder.
Hold the position.
Step back to release the stretch.
keyCues: Do not force the shoulder backward.
completionCriteria: A comfortable chest stretch is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds simple shoulder mobility content.
exercises.description: A controlled cross-body shoulder stretch.
setup: Stand or sit upright.
Bring one arm across the body.
steps: Use the opposite arm to guide the raised arm gently across the chest.
Hold the comfortable stretch.
Release and switch sides.
keyCues: Do not force the elbow across the body.
completionCriteria: The comfortable stretch is held for the prescribed duration on the target side.

exercises.name: Figure-4 Glute Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a distinct hip/glute mobility option.
exercises.description: A supine figure-four stretch emphasizing the outer hip and gluteal region.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh.
steps: Gently draw the uncrossed leg toward you until a comfortable stretch is felt.
Hold the position.
Release and switch sides.
keyCues: Stop before the stretch becomes sharp or forced.
completionCriteria: The comfortable figure-four stretch is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds another simple mobility option to the permanent library.
exercises.description: A gentle overhead triceps stretch using controlled arm positioning.
setup: Stand or sit upright.
Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow.
steps: Let the hand travel down behind the head.
Use the opposite hand only as needed for a gentle stretch.
Hold and release.
keyCues: Do not force the elbow backward.
completionCriteria: A comfortable triceps stretch is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a distinct rotational mobility movement.
exercises.description: A controlled upper-back rotation drill performed from a stable supported position.
setup: Start on hands and knees or another stable supported position.
Place one hand lightly behind the head.
steps: Rotate the upper back to bring the elbow toward the ceiling.
Return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side as prescribed.
keyCues: Keep the hips as still as practical.
completionCriteria: A controlled rotation and return are completed on each repetition.

exercises.name: Cobra Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds another mobility option from the original source catalog.
exercises.description: A gentle prone spinal-extension position performed with the hands supporting as needed.
setup: Lie face down.
Place the hands near the ribs or shoulders.
Keep the legs relaxed.
steps: Gently press or prop the upper trunk upward.
Stop at a comfortable range.
Lower back down with control.
completionCriteria: The upper trunk is lifted into a comfortable extension position and returned under control.

exercises.name: Scapular Wall Slide
exercises.placementRationale: Placed with foundational mobility work because the movement develops shoulder/scapular motion and control rather than a true horizontal pulling pattern.
exercises.description: A wall-supported shoulder and scapular mobility drill emphasizing controlled upward arm movement.
setup: Stand with your back near a wall.
Place the arms against or near the wall in a comfortable bent position.
steps: Slide the arms upward as far as the wall position allows without forcing the range.
Return the arms under control.
keyCues: Use the range you can control.
completionCriteria: The arms move upward and return with controlled shoulder motion.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds controlled rotational hip mobility with greater coordination than the earlier foundational mobility exercises.
exercises.description: A seated hip-rotation mobility movement moving between two controlled 90/90 leg positions.
setup: Sit with both legs bent in a 90/90-style position.
Keep the hands on the floor as needed for support.
steps: Rotate the knees and hips together toward the opposite side.
Settle into the new position without forcing the range.
Return through center and repeat.
keyCues: Use your hands for support as needed.
completionCriteria: The legs transition between the two positions under control.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a coordinated multi-position mobility sequence.
exercises.description: A multi-position mobility sequence combining a lunge, hip mobility, and upper-body rotation.
setup: Start in a standing position with clear space.
steps: Step into a controlled lunge.
Place the hands for support and rotate the upper body toward the front leg as comfortable.
Return to standing and switch sides.
completionCriteria: One controlled sequence is completed on the target side and the player returns to standing.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Pry
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a more coordinated lower-body mobility movement after foundational squat and hip mobility work.
exercises.description: A supported deep-squat mobility drill using gentle movement within a comfortable range.
setup: Stand with a stable, comfortable stance.
Lower into a deep squat only as far as the range allows comfortably.
Use support if needed.
steps: Shift gently within the squat to explore the hip and ankle range.
Return to standing under control.
keyCues: Do not force the knees or hips.
completionCriteria: The player completes the controlled pry sequence and returns to standing.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
exercises.placementRationale: Adds controlled thoracic rotation and shoulder mobility.
exercises.description: A quadruped upper-back rotation movement with one arm reaching underneath the body.
setup: Start on hands and knees.
Keep the hips stacked over the knees as comfortably as possible.
steps: Reach one arm underneath the torso toward the opposite side.
Rotate back to open the chest and return the arm.
Repeat on the other side.
completionCriteria: The arm reaches under the body and returns through a controlled range.

exercises.name: Seated 90/90 Fold
exercises.placementRationale: Expands the 90/90 mobility family with a more involved positional movement.
exercises.description: A seated 90/90 hip-position stretch with a gentle forward fold.
setup: Sit in a 90/90-style hip position.
Place the hands where they can support the body.
steps: Hinge forward over the front leg until a comfortable stretch is felt.
Hold briefly.
Return upright and switch sides.
completionCriteria: The comfortable forward-fold position is held for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Couch Quad Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a more involved quadriceps and hip-flexor mobility option.
exercises.description: A supported quadriceps stretch using a wall or couch for the rear leg.
setup: Kneel with one knee close to a stable surface.
Place the lower leg or foot behind you in the supported position.
Keep the front foot stable.
steps: Bring the torso upright as tolerated.
Hold the gentle quadriceps stretch.
Return carefully and switch sides.
keyCues: Do not force the knee or hip range.
completionCriteria: The supported quadriceps stretch is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Pigeon Stretch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a distinct hip-focused mobility option.
exercises.description: A supported hip stretch using a bent front leg and extended rear leg.
setup: Set up in a supported pigeon-like position with the front leg bent and rear leg extended behind.
Use the hands or a support to reduce load as needed.
steps: Settle into the position gradually.
Maintain the comfortable stretch.
Return slowly and switch sides.
keyCues: Do not force the hip range.
completionCriteria: The supported stretch position is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Deep Lunge Rotation
exercises.placementRationale: Combines hip-position mobility with controlled thoracic rotation.
exercises.description: A controlled lunge-based mobility movement with an upper-body rotation.
setup: Step into a comfortable lunge stance.
Place one hand near the front foot for support.
steps: Rotate the upper trunk toward the front leg.
Return to center and step back.
Repeat on the other side.
completionCriteria: A controlled lunge rotation is completed on the target side.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.description: A horizontal push performed with the hands elevated on a stable surface.
setup: Place your hands on a stable elevated surface.
Extend the legs behind you and create a straight body line.
steps: Bend the elbows to lower the chest toward the surface.
Press through the hands to return to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The body lowers toward the support.
The player presses back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Assisted Squat
exercises.description: An assisted bodyweight squat using a stable support for balance.
setup: Stand facing or beside a stable support.
Hold the support lightly.
steps: Bend the knees and hips to lower into a comfortable squat.
Use the support only as needed.
Press through the feet to return to standing.
keyCues: Use the support for balance, not to pull yourself upward.
completionCriteria: A controlled squat and return to standing are completed.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Good Morning
exercises.description: A standing hip-hinge pattern performed without external load.
setup: Stand with feet about hip-width apart.
Keep the knees softly bent and the trunk tall.
steps: Push the hips backward while the trunk inclines forward.
Stop at a controlled range.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing.
completionCriteria: The hips move backward through a controlled hinge.
The player returns fully upright.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge March
exercises.description: A glute-bridge position with controlled alternating foot lifts.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet planted.
Lift into a bridge position.
steps: Keep the hips elevated.
Lift one foot slightly without letting the pelvis rotate.
Return the foot and alternate sides.
Lower the hips when finished.
completionCriteria: Each alternating foot lift is completed without a major pelvic shift.

exercises.name: Supported Split Squat
exercises.description: A supported split-squat position using external support for balance.
setup: Stand in a staggered stance beside a stable support.
Hold the support lightly.
steps: Lower the body by bending both knees.
Keep most of the load on the front leg.
Press through the front foot to return to the start.
keyCues: Use the support only as needed.
completionCriteria: The player lowers and returns through a controlled split-squat range.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance
exercises.description: An independent single-leg balance exercise performed without external support.
setup: Stand upright with clear floor space.
Place your feet under you.
steps: Shift weight onto one leg.
Lift the opposite foot from the floor.
Maintain the position with controlled posture.
Return the lifted foot gently.
keyCues: Look at a stable point if helpful.
completionCriteria: One foot remains off the floor for the prescribed hold duration.
The player returns safely to two-foot stance.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: A standard dead-bug pattern emphasizing control of the trunk while the limbs move.
setup: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent.
Raise the arms and legs to a comfortable starting position.
steps: Lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to the start.
Alternate sides.
keyCues: Use a range that preserves trunk control.
completionCriteria: Each opposite-arm/opposite-leg cycle is completed without losing trunk control.

exercises.name: Forearm Plank
exercises.description: A full-length forearm plank emphasizing active trunk stabilization.
setup: Place your forearms on the floor.
Extend your legs behind you.
Position the body in a straight supported line.
steps: Brace the trunk.
Maintain the plank position.
Lower the knees when the prescribed hold is complete.
keyCues: Do not sag through the lower back.
completionCriteria: The full plank position is established.
The prescribed hold duration is completed with controlled alignment.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Reach
exercises.placementRationale: Challenges the trunk to resist rotation during unilateral upper-limb movement from a stable plank base.
exercises.description: A high-plank anti-rotation exercise using alternating controlled reaches.
setup: Start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders.
Set the feet wide enough to allow controlled movement.
steps: Lift one hand and reach forward.
Return the hand to the floor.
Alternate sides.
keyCues: Use a stance that allows control.
completionCriteria: Each hand lifts and returns without a major trunk rotation.

exercises.name: Side Plank from Knees
exercises.description: A short-lever side plank performed with the knees supported.
setup: Lie on your side with knees bent.
Position the supporting forearm beneath the shoulder.
steps: Lift the hips from the floor.
Maintain the side-supported position.
Lower with control.
keyCues: Keep the head and trunk aligned.
Press the forearm into the floor.
Keep the hips lifted without rolling forward.
completionCriteria: The side-plank position is established.
The prescribed hold duration is completed with the knees remaining supported.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.description: A controlled lower-trunk flexion movement performed from a supine position.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet lightly off the floor.
Place the arms beside you for support.
steps: Curl the pelvis and knees toward the ribcage using the trunk.
Return the feet or legs toward the starting position without swinging.
completionCriteria: The pelvis lifts from the floor under control.
The player returns to the start without swinging.

exercises.name: Step-and-Reach
exercises.description: A coordinated stepping pattern paired with a controlled reaching action.
setup: Stand with clear space around you.
Begin with the feet comfortably together.
steps: Step forward or diagonally while reaching with the opposite arm.
Return to the starting stance.
Alternate sides.
keyCues: Coordinate the step and reach smoothly.
completionCriteria: The step and coordinated reach are completed and the player returns to a stable stance.

exercises.name: Supported Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description: A single-leg calf raise performed while using a stable support for balance.
setup: Stand beside a stable support.
Place most of your weight on one leg.
Use one or both hands lightly as needed.
steps: Rise onto the ball of the working foot.
Lower the heel with control.
Repeat on the same side before switching as prescribed.
keyCues: Keep the working foot pointed forward.
completionCriteria: The working heel rises and lowers through the controlled range.

exercises.name: Alternating Heel Slide
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses the bilateral heel-slide pattern into alternating unilateral hamstring control.
exercises.description: An alternating version of the supine heel-slide hamstring pattern.
setup: Lie on your back with both heels on a sliding surface.
Keep the trunk relaxed but controlled.
steps: Slide one heel toward the body.
Return it to the starting position.
Alternate to the other leg.
keyCues: Move one leg at a time.
completionCriteria: Each heel bends and returns through a controlled range.

exercises.name: Knee Push-Up
exercises.description: A floor-based horizontal push performed with the knees supported.
setup: Place your hands on the floor under or slightly outside the shoulders.
Place your knees on the floor behind the hips.
Align the trunk from shoulders toward knees.
steps: Bend the elbows to lower the chest.
Keep the body aligned.
Press through the hands to return to the start.
completionCriteria: The chest lowers close to the floor while the elbows bend under control.
The player presses back to the straight-arm starting position.

exercises.name: Prone Elbow Draw
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a foundational upper-back and scapular pulling pattern late in Tier 1 so the initial exercise library includes a basic pulling counterpart to the early pushing patterns.
exercises.description: A prone upper-back movement using controlled elbow drawing without external resistance.
setup: Lie face down with the arms extended or slightly angled forward.
Keep the legs and hips comfortably supported.
steps: Draw the elbows toward the ribs while gently lifting the upper chest as appropriate.
Return the arms forward under control.
completionCriteria: The elbows draw back and return through a controlled range.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.description: A standard bodyweight squat performed from standing.
setup: Stand with your feet in a comfortable stance.
Keep both feet planted.
steps: Bend the knees and hips to lower your body through a controlled range.
Press through your feet to return to standing.
completionCriteria: The lowering phase is completed through a comfortable controlled range.
The player returns fully to standing.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.description: A supported isometric squat position held with the back against a wall.
setup: Stand with your back against a clear wall.
Place your feet far enough forward to allow a comfortable squat position.
steps: Slide the back down the wall into a comfortable squat position.
Maintain the position.
Press through the feet to stand when the hold ends.
keyCues: Maintain a comfortable knee and hip angle.
Do not rush into the position.
completionCriteria: The wall-supported squat position is established.
The prescribed hold duration is completed with the back supported.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: An independent reverse lunge performed from standing.
setup: Stand upright with feet comfortably under you.
Keep clear space behind you.
steps: Step one foot backward.
Lower under control by bending both knees.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Alternate sides.
completionCriteria: The step-back, lowering phase, and return are completed under control.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.description: A controlled step-up onto a stable low step.
setup: Stand facing a stable low step or platform.
Place the working foot fully on the step.
steps: Push through the working foot to rise onto the step.
Bring the other foot up as needed.
Step back down under control.
Alternate as prescribed.
keyCues: Keep the working foot fully supported.
completionCriteria: The player rises onto and returns from the stable step under control.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Reach
exercises.description: A single-leg balance movement combining a controlled reach toward a target direction.
setup: Stand upright with clear floor space.
Shift weight onto one leg.
steps: Lift the other foot from the floor.
Reach the free leg or body toward the target direction without losing balance.
Return to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The reach is completed and the player returns to stable single-leg balance.

exercises.name: High Plank
exercises.description: A full-length high plank emphasizing active trunk stability.
setup: Place your hands on the floor under the shoulders.
Extend the legs behind you.
Set the body in a straight line.
steps: Brace the trunk and maintain the position.
Hold for the prescribed duration.
Lower the knees when finished.
completionCriteria: The full high-plank position is established.
The prescribed hold duration is completed with controlled alignment.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses anti-rotation control by adding repeated unilateral hand removal from the plank base.
exercises.description: A high-plank anti-rotation movement using alternating shoulder taps.
setup: Start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders.
Use a stance that allows the hips to stay controlled.
steps: Lift one hand to touch the opposite shoulder.
Return the hand to the floor.
Alternate sides.
keyCues: Keep the pelvis as level as possible.
Move slowly enough to control rotation.
Maintain a stable support foot position.
completionCriteria: Each hand taps the opposite shoulder and returns without a major trunk shift.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: A full side plank performed with the legs extended.
setup: Lie on your side.
Position the supporting forearm beneath the shoulder.
Extend the legs into a stacked or comfortable side-supported position.
steps: Lift the hips from the floor.
Maintain the side-plank position.
Lower under control.
keyCues: Keep the hips elevated without twisting.
completionCriteria: The full side-plank position is established.
The prescribed hold duration is completed with the legs supported in the full position.

exercises.name: Sit-Up
exercises.description: A controlled sit-up performed from a supine starting position.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet supported.
Place the hands lightly behind the head or across the chest.
steps: Curl the trunk upward until the torso reaches an upright or near-upright seated position.
Lower back down under control.
completionCriteria: The torso reaches an upright or near-upright seated position.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: An alternating trunk-flexion and rotation movement performed from a supine position.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and hands lightly behind the head.
Lift the head and shoulders slightly.
steps: Bring one knee toward the trunk while rotating the opposite side of the upper trunk toward it.
Return toward center and switch sides.
keyCues: Rotate through the trunk rather than pulling the head.
completionCriteria: Each alternating side completes a controlled flexion-and-rotation cycle.

exercises.name: Step Jack
exercises.description: A low-impact jumping-jack pattern performed with alternating steps instead of jumps.
setup: Stand upright with feet comfortably together or close.
Keep the arms relaxed and ready to move.
steps: Step one foot outward while moving the arms upward.
Return that foot toward center while lowering the arms.
Repeat on the opposite side.
completionCriteria: The alternating step-jack pattern continues for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description: An independent single-leg calf raise performed without external support.
setup: Stand upright with clear space.
Shift most of your weight onto one leg.
Use the free leg lightly for balance only if needed.
steps: Rise onto the ball of the working foot.
Reach a controlled top position.
Lower the heel back down.
completionCriteria: The working heel rises and returns through the controlled range.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces the standard full-body horizontal push after wall, incline, and knee-supported progressions.
exercises.description: A standard floor-based push-up in which the body is maintained in a controlled straight-line position.
setup: Place your hands on the floor at a comfortable width.
Extend your legs behind you and establish a stable starting position.
steps: Bend your elbows to lower your body with control.
Lower through your comfortable controlled range while maintaining body alignment.
Press through your hands to return to the starting position.
keyCues: Move smoothly through a consistent range.
completionCriteria: A controlled lowering phase is completed.
The player returns to the established starting position.

exercises.name: Alternating Lunge
exercises.placementRationale: Builds from reverse-lunge and split-squat foundations into repeated alternating unilateral stepping.
exercises.description: A repeated reverse-stepping lunge pattern performed by alternating legs.
setup: Stand upright with feet in a comfortable stance.
Clear enough space behind you to step safely.
steps: Step one foot backward and lower under control.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Repeat with the opposite leg.
completionCriteria: A controlled lunge is completed on one side.
The player returns to the standing stance before alternating.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Moves from supported unilateral work toward independently controlled split-stance strength.
exercises.description: A stationary split-stance lower-body movement performed with one leg forward and one leg behind.
setup: Stand in a comfortable split stance.
Keep enough space between the feet to remain balanced.
steps: Lower your body by bending both knees.
Descend through a comfortable controlled range.
Press through the front foot to return to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The player completes a controlled lowering phase.
The player returns to the established split stance.

exercises.name: Kickstand Hip Hinge
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces asymmetrical loading and balance demands while retaining a broad base of support.
exercises.description: A hip-hinge movement performed from a staggered stance with most of the work carried by the lead leg.
setup: Stand with one foot slightly behind the other.
Keep the stance stable and comfortable.
steps: Shift your hips backward while keeping the trunk controlled.
Move into a comfortable hinge range.
Drive through the lead foot to return upright.
keyCues: Use the rear foot mainly for balance.
completionCriteria: The player reaches the controlled hinge position.
The player returns to upright standing.

exercises.name: Wall Pike Lean
exercises.placementRationale: First Tier 2 vertical-push pattern; introduces the pike position without immediately requiring repeated pressing.
exercises.description: A wall-assisted pike-position lean that develops overhead pressing posture and shoulder control.
setup: Set up facing away from or beside a stable wall, with the hands on a stable surface and the body in a controlled pike position.
Place the hands on a stable surface and establish a controlled pike position.
steps: Shift the shoulders into the pike position while keeping the body organized.
Hold the established lean without collapsing through the shoulders.
Return to the starting position under control.
keyCues: Use the wall only as intended for support.
completionCriteria: The player establishes a controlled pike lean with the shoulders shifted forward and the hips elevated.
The position is maintained under control for the prescribed hold.

exercises.name: Plank Up-Down
exercises.placementRationale: Adds controlled load transfer and upper-body coordination to the established plank family.
exercises.description: A plank transition in which the player moves between forearm and hand support while maintaining trunk control.
setup: Start in a stable plank position on the forearms.
Set the feet and trunk in a controlled position.
steps: Move one hand into support and then the other.
Press into a high plank position without excessive trunk rotation.
Return to forearm support under control.
keyCues: Move one arm at a time.
completionCriteria: The player reaches the high support position.
The player returns to forearm support with control.

exercises.name: Bear Hold
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a more demanding trunk position while remaining stationary.
exercises.description: A static quadrupedal hold with the knees hovering and the trunk maintained in a stable position.
setup: Start on hands and knees with hands beneath the shoulders.
Position the knees beneath the hips and prepare to lift them slightly.
steps: Lift the knees just clear of the floor.
Maintain the quadrupedal position without shifting excessively.
Lower the knees back to the floor.
keyCues: Lift the knees only as much as the position requires.
completionCriteria: The knees remain just clear of the floor while the hands, feet, and trunk stay stable.
The prescribed hold duration is completed.

exercises.name: Side Plank Reach
exercises.placementRationale: Builds from the Tier 1 knee-supported lateral stability work by adding controlled upper-body movement.
exercises.description: A side-plank variation in which the upper arm reaches while the trunk remains stable.
setup: Set up in a stable side-plank position.
Place the supporting arm and feet in a comfortable position.
steps: Establish the side plank.
Reach the top arm away from the body while keeping the trunk lifted and stable.
Return the arm while maintaining the support position.
keyCues: Avoid rotating or dropping the hips.
completionCriteria: The side-plank position is established.
The reach and return are completed under control.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a more demanding lower-limb movement against trunk-control requirements.
exercises.description: A lying leg-raise movement in which the legs are lifted and lowered under trunk control.
setup: Lie on your back with the legs extended or comfortably positioned.
Place the arms in a stable supporting position.
steps: Raise the straight legs until they approach a controlled vertical position over the hips.
Keep the trunk stable as the legs rise.
Lower the legs under control until they return near the starting floor position.
keyCues: Use a range that can be maintained without losing position.
completionCriteria: The legs reach a controlled near-vertical position without losing trunk control.
The player returns to the starting position with control.

exercises.name: Controlled Mountain Climber
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces dynamic alternating lower-limb movement from a supported upper-body position before faster mountain-climber work.
exercises.description: A controlled alternating mountain-climber pattern performed from a stable floor position.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position.
Place the hands securely under the shoulders.
steps: Bring one knee forward in a controlled manner.
Return the leg to the starting position.
Repeat on the opposite side.
completionCriteria: The alternating knee-drive pattern is completed as prescribed.

exercises.name: Heel Walk
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a distinct ankle-control pattern without requiring impact.
exercises.description: A walking pattern performed with the forefoot raised while stepping under control.
setup: Stand upright in a clear walking space.
Lift the forefoot so the heels remain the primary contact point.
steps: Step forward while maintaining the heel-supported position.
Continue walking with controlled steps.
completionCriteria: The player maintains the heel-supported walking pattern for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a meaningful hand-position variation after the standard push-up.
exercises.description: A standard floor push-up performed with a wider-than-usual hand position.
setup: Place your hands on the floor wider than shoulder width as comfortable.
Extend your legs behind you into a stable starting position.
steps: Lower the body by bending the elbows.
Move through a controlled range.
Press back to the starting position.
keyCues: Use a comfortable range of motion.
completionCriteria: A controlled lowering phase is completed.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Pike Shrug
exercises.placementRationale: Develops active shoulder elevation and control in the pike position before full pike pressing.
exercises.description: A pike-position shoulder movement emphasizing active shoulder elevation and control.
setup: Establish a stable pike position with the hands supported on the floor.
Set the feet and hips so the shoulders can move freely.
steps: Press the shoulders away from the floor.
Allow the shoulders to lower under control.
Repeat the shoulder movement without collapsing the pike position.
completionCriteria: The shoulders complete a controlled elevation and return.

exercises.name: Prone Row Lift
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses the prone pulling pattern with greater upper-back and arm movement.
exercises.description: A prone upper-back pulling movement in which the arms draw toward the body while the torso remains supported.
setup: Lie face down on a clear floor surface.
Extend the arms comfortably in front of or slightly away from you.
steps: Draw the elbows and arms back in a controlled rowing motion.
Lift the upper body or arms only as required by the movement.
Return the arms to the starting position.
keyCues: Lead with the upper back and elbows.
completionCriteria: The arms complete the controlled pulling motion.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Wide Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a meaningfully different bilateral squat stance and control demand.
exercises.description: A bodyweight squat performed from a wider stance while maintaining controlled knee and hip movement.
setup: Stand with the feet wider than a standard squat stance.
Turn the feet outward only as comfortable.
steps: Bend the knees and hips to lower the body.
Move through a comfortable controlled range.
Press through the feet to return upright.
keyCues: Keep the knees tracking comfortably with the feet.
completionCriteria: The player completes a controlled descent.
The player returns fully to standing.

exercises.name: Side Lunge
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces lateral unilateral lower-body movement distinct from forward and backward lunging.
exercises.description: A lateral lunge pattern that shifts bodyweight toward one bent leg while the opposite leg remains more extended.
setup: Stand upright with feet comfortably apart.
Clear space to each side.
steps: Step or shift to one side and bend the receiving leg.
Lower into a comfortable lateral lunge position.
Push through the receiving foot to return to the center.
completionCriteria: The player reaches the controlled lateral lunge.
The player returns to the centered stance.

exercises.name: Step-Down
exercises.placementRationale: Adds controlled unilateral lowering and greater single-leg control.
exercises.description: A controlled single-leg lowering movement performed from an elevated surface.
setup: Stand on a stable low step or platform.
Place one foot near the edge while keeping the other ready to move.
steps: Bend the standing leg to lower the free foot toward the floor.
Lightly reach the free foot downward without collapsing.
Drive through the standing foot to return up.
keyCues: Use the support surface only as high as appropriate.
Lower slowly enough to remain balanced.
completionCriteria: The free foot reaches the prescribed lower position.
The player returns to the starting standing position.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses from bilateral bridge work to unilateral hip extension with a stable floor position.
exercises.description: A single-leg glute-bridge movement in which one leg remains actively supported while the hips extend.
setup: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg extended in line with the body.
Place the supporting foot firmly on the floor.
steps: Press through the supporting foot to lift the hips.
Maintain a stable pelvis at the top.
Lower the hips back down under control.
completionCriteria: The hips lift into the controlled bridge position.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hinge Reach
exercises.placementRationale: Combines single-leg balance with controlled hip hinging without introducing speed or impact.
exercises.description: A single-leg balance and hinge movement combined with a controlled reach toward the floor or forward space.
setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg free to move.
Establish a stable balance before hinging.
steps: Hinge forward from the standing hip.
Reach with the hands while the free leg moves behind you for balance.
Return to upright standing without losing control.
keyCues: Move slowly enough to maintain balance.
completionCriteria: The player completes the controlled reach position.
The player returns to upright single-leg balance.

exercises.name: Heel-Slide Dead Bug
exercises.placementRationale: Adds controlled limb excursion to the established Dead Bug progression.
exercises.description: A dead-bug variation in which the heel slides away while the trunk remains braced and stable.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet supported.
Position the arms as needed for a stable dead-bug setup.
steps: Brace the trunk gently.
Slide one heel away from the body while keeping the trunk controlled.
Return the heel and alternate sides.
keyCues: Move one leg at a time.
completionCriteria: The heel reaches the controlled extended position.
The leg returns before the opposite side moves.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Tuck
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a dynamic seated trunk-flexion pattern with increased coordination.
exercises.description: A seated trunk-and-hip flexion movement that draws the knees toward the torso while balancing under control.
setup: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet positioned to allow movement.
Place the hands where needed for a stable starting position.
steps: Lean back slightly while keeping the trunk controlled.
Draw the knees toward the torso.
Extend the legs back to the starting position without losing control.
completionCriteria: The knees are drawn toward the torso.
The player returns to the seated starting position.

exercises.name: Toe Touch
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a larger controlled trunk-flexion movement while remaining straightforward to coordinate.
exercises.description: A standing or seated forward-flexion movement in which the hands reach toward the feet through a controlled range.
setup: Stand or sit with the legs comfortably arranged and the feet accessible for a controlled forward reach.
Keep enough space to move without obstruction.
steps: Hinge or flex forward toward the feet.
Reach through a comfortable range without forcing the motion.
Return to the starting position under control.
completionCriteria: The hands reach the toes or lower legs without forcing the forward-flexion range.
The player returns under control.

exercises.name: Flutter Kick
exercises.placementRationale: Adds continuous alternating lower-limb movement requiring sustained trunk control.
exercises.description: An alternating straight-leg kicking movement performed while maintaining a controlled trunk position.
setup: Lie on your back and establish a stable trunk position.
Extend the legs in a manageable range.
steps: Lift the legs slightly from the starting position.
Alternate small controlled up-and-down leg movements.
Stop and return to the starting position when the set ends.
completionCriteria: The alternating kicking pattern is completed as prescribed.

exercises.name: Scissor Kick
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a crossing-leg variation with a distinct coordination demand within the lower-trunk movement family.
exercises.description: An alternating leg-crossing movement performed while maintaining trunk control.
setup: Lie on your back and establish a stable trunk position.
Extend the legs in a manageable range.
steps: Lift the legs slightly.
Cross and uncross the legs in a controlled alternating pattern.
Return to the starting position when complete.
completionCriteria: The alternating crossing pattern is completed as prescribed.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a dedicated seated rotational pattern after the simpler Tier 1 cross-body control work.
exercises.description: A seated rotational movement in which the trunk turns from side to side while maintaining controlled posture.
setup: Sit with knees bent and feet arranged for a stable base.
Lean the trunk to a comfortable position for rotation.
steps: Rotate the trunk toward one side.
Return through center and rotate toward the other side.
Continue the alternating pattern under control.
keyCues: Rotate through the trunk rather than only the arms.
completionCriteria: The trunk completes a controlled rotation to one side and returns through center.
The alternating sequence continues as prescribed.

exercises.name: Sit-Through
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces rotational movement integrated with weight-bearing and locomotor coordination.
exercises.description: A supported floor transition in which one leg moves through the hands while the trunk rotates and the body remains controlled.
setup: Start in a stable quadrupedal or bear-like support position.
Place the hands firmly on the floor.
steps: Shift weight through the supporting limbs.
Rotate and extend one leg through the space beside the hands.
Return the leg and repeat on the opposite side.
completionCriteria: The leg passes through the support position.
The player returns to the starting support before switching sides.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses the controlled mountain-climber pattern into a more continuous locomotor movement.
exercises.description: An alternating mountain-climber pattern performed from a stable high-plank position with continuous controlled leg action.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position.
Place the hands securely under the shoulders.
steps: Drive one knee forward.
Return it to the starting position.
Alternate to the opposite leg in a controlled rhythm.
completionCriteria: The prescribed alternating knee-drive sequence is completed.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces whole-body crawling coordination after the stationary Bear Hold.
exercises.description: A controlled quadrupedal locomotion pattern in which the hands and feet move the body forward.
setup: Start in a bear position with hands and feet supporting the body.
Lift the knees slightly clear of the floor into a stable bear position.
steps: Move one hand and the opposite foot forward.
Continue alternating limbs to travel forward.
Reverse or stop as prescribed while maintaining control.
completionCriteria: The prescribed crawling distance or duration is completed.

exercises.name: Crab Walk
setupRequirements: stable floor with sufficient clearance for quadrupedal travel
exercises.placementRationale: Restores the foundational crab locomotion pattern before the more demanding Crab Reach introduced in Tier 3C.
exercises.description: A quadrupedal locomotion pattern performed while facing upward and moving laterally or forward with hands and feet supporting the body.
setup: Sit with the feet on the floor and hands behind you.
Lift the hips into a stable crab position.
steps: Move one hand and the opposite foot to begin traveling.
Continue alternating the limbs to travel laterally or forward while maintaining the crab position.
Lower the hips when finished.
completionCriteria: The prescribed crawling pattern is completed for the assigned work.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a substantially more demanding hand position after the standard and wide-grip push-up stages.
exercises.description: A floor push-up performed with the hands placed close together beneath the chest to increase the triceps-dominant pressing demand.
setup: Place your hands close together on the floor beneath the chest area.
Extend your legs behind you into a stable starting position.
steps: Bend the elbows to lower your body under control.
Use a comfortable range while maintaining trunk alignment.
Press through the hands to return to the starting position.
keyCues: Use a range that preserves stable form.
completionCriteria: A controlled lowering phase is completed.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: First repeated vertical pressing movement after wall pike work and pike shrug control.
exercises.description: A pike push-up in which the shoulders travel toward the floor from an elevated hip position.
setup: Start in a stable pike position with hands on the floor.
Set the feet and hips so the body forms an inverted V shape.
steps: Bend the elbows to lower the head and shoulders toward the floor.
Press through the hands to return to the pike position.
completionCriteria: The head moves toward the floor between the hands with the elbows clearly bent.
The player returns to the pike starting position.

exercises.name: Prone W Raise
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a more demanding upper-back and scapular-control configuration.
exercises.description: A prone scapular-control movement in which the arms lift into a W-shaped position to develop upper-back control.
setup: Lie face down with the arms positioned in a W shape or ready to move into it.
Keep the forehead and torso comfortably supported.
steps: Draw the elbows toward the sides while lifting the hands or forearms slightly.
Pause briefly in the controlled W position.
Lower the arms back to the starting position.
keyCues: Do not jerk the arms upward.
completionCriteria: The arms reach the controlled W position.
The player returns the arms to the starting position.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlift
exercises.placementRationale: Combines single-leg balance with a substantial unilateral hinge demand.
exercises.description: A single-leg hip-hinge movement performed while the free leg extends backward for balance.
setup: Stand on one leg with the standing foot stable.
Position the free leg ready to move behind you.
steps: Hinge forward from the standing hip.
Extend the free leg backward as the trunk lowers.
Drive through the standing foot to return upright.
completionCriteria: The player reaches the controlled hinge position.
The player returns to upright single-leg standing.

exercises.name: Staggered Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces asymmetric hand positioning and uneven loading after the Tier 2 standard, wide, and diamond push-up pathways.
exercises.description: A push-up performed with the hands offset to create an asymmetric loading pattern.
setup: Place your hands on the floor with one hand slightly forward of the other.
Extend your legs behind you and establish a stable starting position.
steps: Lower your body with control while keeping the staggered hand positions.
Press through both hands to return to the starting position.
Repeat with the prescribed hand orientation.
completionCriteria: The chest lowers toward the floor with the staggered hand positions maintained.
The player returns to the starting position without losing the staggered setup.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Increases upper-body loading through a changed body angle without immediately requiring the unilateral demands of an archer push-up.
exercises.description: A push-up performed with the feet elevated on a stable surface, increasing upper-body loading.
setup: Place your hands on the floor in a comfortable push-up width.
Place your feet on a stable elevated surface.
Set a controlled starting position.
steps: Lower your body toward the floor with control.
Press through your hands to return to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The chest lowers toward the floor with the elevated feet remaining stable.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Elevated Pike Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Builds on the Tier 2 pike push-up with greater shoulder-loading leverage before later high-skill vertical pressing.
exercises.description: A feet-elevated pike push-up that increases shoulder-loading demand.
setup: Place your hands on the floor.
Place your feet on a stable elevated surface and raise the hips into a pike.
steps: Bend the elbows and lower the head and shoulders toward the floor.
Press through the hands to return to the pike position.
completionCriteria: The head moves toward the floor between the hands with the elbows clearly bent.
The player returns to the pike position.

exercises.name: Reverse Snow Angel
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a larger controlled scapular and upper-back movement pattern after prone elbow draw, prone row lift, and W raise.
exercises.description: A prone upper-back movement in which the arms sweep through a wide arc while the trunk stays controlled.
setup: Lie face down with the legs extended comfortably.
Position the arms so they can move through a wide arc.
steps: Lift the arms slightly from the floor.
Sweep the arms through a wide controlled arc and return them to the starting position.
Return the arms to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The arms complete the controlled sweep and return to the starting position.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raise
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a distinct overhead scapular-control position without requiring external resistance.
exercises.description: A prone scapular-control movement with the arms arranged in a Y position.
setup: Lie face down with the legs extended comfortably.
Extend the arms forward and slightly outward into a Y.
steps: Lift the arms into the Y-shaped position until the hands clear the floor under control.
Lower them back to the floor with control.
completionCriteria: The arms reach the Y-shaped position with the hands lifted clear of the floor.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces substantial multiplanar lower-body control and lateral range after Tier 2 bilateral squat development.
exercises.description: A lateral squat pattern in which one knee bends while the opposite leg extends to the side.
setup: Stand in a wide, stable stance.
Keep both feet planted.
steps: Shift toward one side and bend that knee.
Keep the opposite leg extended as comfortable.
Push through the working foot to return toward center and switch sides.
completionCriteria: The hips lower toward the working side until the working thigh approaches parallel with the floor while the opposite leg remains extended.
The player returns toward the starting stance under control.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces intentional jumping and landing as a new movement capability after foundational squat control.
exercises.description: A squat followed by controlled vertical propulsion and a stable landing.
setup: Stand with feet in a comfortable stance.
Clear the surrounding area.
steps: Lower into a controlled squat.
Drive through the feet to jump.
Land softly and regain a stable position.
completionCriteria: The player completes the jump from the squat.
The landing is controlled and stable.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge
exercises.placementRationale: Adds diagonal and multiplanar unilateral stepping after forward, backward, split-stance, and lateral patterns.
exercises.description: A diagonal lunge in which one leg steps behind and across the body.
setup: Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart.
Leave space for a diagonal step behind.
steps: Step one leg diagonally behind the other.
Lower under control with the front foot stable.
Push through the front foot to return to standing and switch sides.
completionCriteria: The diagonal lowering phase is completed.
The player returns to standing under control.

exercises.name: Hamstring Walkout
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a substantially more demanding posterior-chain movement through controlled extension and return.
exercises.description: A posterior-chain movement that gradually lengthens the leg position from a bridge and returns under control.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet planted.
Lift the hips into a comfortable bridge.
steps: Walk the feet away in small controlled steps.
Stop at the furthest controlled position.
Walk the feet back and lower the hips.
keyCues: Do not force the end range.
completionCriteria: The feet walk away from the body through the controlled walkout range and return under control.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Quarter Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Combines unilateral balance with controlled knee and hip flexion after single-leg balance and reach work.
exercises.description: A shallow single-leg squat emphasizing controlled knee and hip flexion while maintaining balance.
setup: Stand on one leg near a stable support if needed.
Find a stable upright starting position.
steps: Bend the supporting knee and hip into a shallow squat.
Maintain balance through the lower position.
Press through the foot to return to standing and switch sides.
completionCriteria: The supporting leg reaches a shallow squat position while the foot remains stable and the body stays balanced.
The player returns to stable single-leg standing.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Clock Reach
exercises.placementRationale: Expands single-leg balance into controlled movement in multiple directions.
exercises.description: A single-leg balance movement combining a stable base with controlled reaches in multiple directions.
setup: Stand tall on one leg.
Keep a stable support nearby if needed.
steps: Reach toward a selected clock-face direction while keeping the standing foot stable.
Return to center and reach toward the next direction.
Complete the sequence and switch sides as prescribed.
keyCues: Reach only as far as you can control.
completionCriteria: The required directional reaches are completed.
The player returns to a stable single-leg position.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a substantially more demanding long-lever trunk-control position after plank and dead-bug progressions.
exercises.description: A long-lever supine trunk-control position with the limbs extended away from the center of the body.
setup: Lie on your back with the limbs positioned comfortably.
Prepare to establish the hollow-body position.
steps: Extend the arms and legs away from the trunk while maintaining a controlled hollow-body position.
Maintain the position for the prescribed duration.
Return to the starting position with control.
keyCues: Use a lever length you can maintain.
completionCriteria: The hollow-body position is established with the trunk controlled and the lower back maintained against or close to the floor.
The prescribed hold duration is completed without losing the required position.

exercises.name: Boat Hold
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces sustained seated trunk control with a more demanding lever than earlier seated knee-tuck work.
exercises.description: A seated trunk-flexion hold in which the torso and legs are balanced above the floor.
setup: Sit on the floor with the knees bent.
Lift the chest into a balanced seated position.
steps: Lean back slightly while maintaining a controlled trunk.
Lift the feet so the lower legs are elevated while the torso leans back in a controlled V-shaped seated position.
Maintain the position for the prescribed duration.
completionCriteria: The seated V-shaped position is established with the torso and legs balanced under control.
The prescribed hold duration is completed.

exercises.name: Side Plank Knee Drive
exercises.placementRationale: Adds coordinated lower-limb movement to the established side-plank family.
exercises.description: A side-plank variation that adds controlled knee movement while maintaining lateral trunk stability.
setup: Set up in a stable side-plank position.
Align the trunk before moving the upper leg.
steps: Lift into the side plank.
Drive the upper knee toward the chest while keeping the side plank aligned.
Return the leg and lower with control.
completionCriteria: The side-plank position is maintained during the knee movement.
The upper knee reaches the chest-facing position under control.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Oblique Crunch
exercises.placementRationale: Placed in trunk lateral flexion because the primary trunk action is side-bending rather than axial rotation.
exercises.description: A side-lying trunk-flexion movement emphasizing controlled side-bending.
setup: Lie on your side in a comfortable aligned position.
Arrange the legs and supporting arm so the trunk can move freely.
steps: Lift the ribcage toward the pelvis on the upper side of the body.
Contract the side of the trunk to complete the movement.
Lower back with control.
completionCriteria: The side-bending movement is completed.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Lateral Shuffle
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces continuous lateral locomotion and rhythm after basic stepping and low-complexity locomotion.
exercises.description: A continuous side-to-side locomotion pattern using quick, controlled steps.
setup: Stand with knees slightly bent and feet ready to move.
Clear enough space for lateral travel.
steps: Shuffle laterally in one direction.
Reverse direction under control.
Continue the side-to-side pattern for the prescribed duration.
completionCriteria: The player sustains the lateral shuffle pattern for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Hindu Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a distinct full-body pressing path involving controlled shoulder and trunk movement after the established conventional and asymmetric push-up progressions.
