exercises.description: A flowing push-up pattern that moves through a coordinated arcing path.
setup: Place the hands on the floor in a stable position.
Start with the hips elevated.
steps: Shift the shoulders forward and lower the chest through a smooth arcing path.
Continue through the forward portion.
Reverse the pattern to return to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The body completes the controlled forward arc and returns to the starting position.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Side Plank Hip Lift
exercises.placementRationale: Adds repeated lateral hip and trunk movement to the established side-plank stability progression.
exercises.description: A side-plank movement that repeatedly lowers and lifts the hips while maintaining lateral trunk control.
setup: Set up in a stable side plank.
Align the trunk and legs before moving.
steps: Lower the hips with control.
Lift the hips back into the side plank.
Repeat while maintaining alignment.
completionCriteria: The lower hip approaches the floor without collapsing the side plank.
The hips return to the straight-body side-plank position.

exercises.name: Prone T Raise
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a distinct horizontal scapular-control pattern following the Y and W configurations.
exercises.description: A prone scapular-control movement with the arms extended out to the sides in a T position.
setup: Lie face down with the legs extended comfortably.
Extend the arms to the sides in a T position.
steps: Lift the arms with controlled shoulder-blade movement.
Lower the arms back to the floor.
completionCriteria: The arms lift into the T position with the hands clear of the floor.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Prone Swimmer
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces coordinated movement through multiple upper-back and shoulder positions.
exercises.description: A prone coordinated upper-back movement that transitions the arms through multiple positions.
setup: Lie face down with the legs extended comfortably.
Position the arms ready to move through the sequence.
steps: Move the arms from overhead through the swimmer sequence while keeping the torso stable.
Continue the arm path around to the hips and return to overhead.
Return to the starting position.
completionCriteria: The arms complete the full overhead-to-hips-to-overhead swimmer sequence.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Assisted Pistol Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a demanding unilateral squat pattern while retaining assistance.
exercises.description: An assisted deep single-leg squat using external support to control balance and range.
setup: Stand beside a stable support.
Shift your weight onto one leg and extend the other leg forward as comfortable.
steps: Use the support as needed while lowering until the working thigh approaches the floor and the free leg remains extended forward.
Maintain control at the bottom.
Use the support to return to standing.
completionCriteria: The assisted single-leg squat reaches the defined deep position with control.
The player returns to standing with control.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Tiptoe Walk
exercises.placementRationale: Combines unilateral calf control with balance and locomotion.
exercises.description: A continuous walking pattern emphasizing raised-heel balance and unilateral calf control.
setup: Stand in a clear walking area.
Rise onto the balls of the feet as appropriate.
steps: Take controlled steps while maintaining the raised-heel position.
Transfer weight smoothly between feet.
Continue for the prescribed duration.
completionCriteria: The player maintains the tiptoe walking pattern for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: V-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces substantially more demanding combined trunk-flexion and lower-limb control.
exercises.description: A dynamic trunk-compression movement in which the torso and legs rise toward one another.
setup: Lie on your back with the arms and legs extended comfortably.
Prepare to lift the torso and legs together.
steps: Raise the torso and legs toward one another in a controlled V-shaped motion.
Bring the hands toward the feet or shins at the top of the movement.
Lower back to the starting position.
keyCues: Do not jerk into the top position.
completionCriteria: The torso and legs converge with the hands reaching toward the feet or shins.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Bear Shoulder Tap
exercises.placementRationale: Advances trunk anti-rotation through alternating upper-limb movement from the loaded bear position.
exercises.description: A bear-position movement in which one hand taps the opposite shoulder while the trunk resists rotation.
setup: Start on hands and knees.
Lift the knees slightly into the bear position.
steps: Shift weight without rotating the trunk.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder.
Return the hand and alternate sides.
completionCriteria: Each shoulder tap is completed while the bear position remains controlled.

exercises.name: Plank Jack
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces dynamic lateral leg movement from the high-plank position after static and controlled plank progressions.
exercises.description: A dynamic plank movement in which the feet move laterally while the trunk stays controlled.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position.
Place the hands under the shoulders.
steps: Move the feet apart laterally.
Return the feet toward the starting position.
Repeat while maintaining the plank.
completionCriteria: The feet move apart and back together while the trunk remains in a controlled plank position.
The plank position remains controlled.

exercises.name: Skater Jump
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces lateral jumping after the established Skater Step.
exercises.description: A lateral jumping pattern that transfers the body from one leg to the other with controlled landing.
setup: Stand with feet comfortably apart.
Clear space for lateral travel.
steps: Push from one leg to travel laterally.
Land on the opposite leg with control.
Stabilize and repeat to the other side.
completionCriteria: The lateral jump is completed.
The landing is controlled and stable.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge to Knee Drive
exercises.placementRationale: Combines established unilateral lower-body movement with a controlled balance-demanding transition.
exercises.description: A controlled transition from a reverse lunge into a single-leg knee-drive position.
setup: Stand tall with space behind you.
Prepare to step backward.
steps: Step one leg backward into a controlled lunge.
Drive that leg forward and upward into the knee-drive position.
Regain balance before the next repetition.
completionCriteria: The reverse-lunge position is reached.
The knee drive is completed with control.

exercises.name: Squat to Knee Drive
exercises.placementRationale: Combines bilateral squat mechanics with single-leg balance and coordinated movement without requiring a jump.
exercises.description: A squat-to-stand movement that finishes with a controlled single-leg knee drive.
setup: Stand with feet in a comfortable stance.
Keep room to shift onto one leg.
steps: Lower into a controlled squat.
Rise and transfer weight onto one leg.
Drive the opposite knee upward and return to the starting stance.
keyCues: Stand tall before the knee drive.
completionCriteria: The squat depth is completed.
The knee drive is completed from stable support.

exercises.name: Assisted Skater Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Aligned with Skater Squat because the assisted and unassisted movements represent the same unilateral squat pathway, with assistance serving as the progression step.
exercises.description: An assisted single-leg squat pattern using support to control the skater-squat position.
setup: Stand beside a stable support.
Shift weight onto one leg and position the free leg behind.
steps: Use the support as needed while lowering into the skater-squat pattern.
Keep the working foot planted.
Use the support to return to standing.
completionCriteria: The supporting leg reaches a controlled skater-squat depth while the rear leg remains positioned behind the body.
The player returns to standing with control.

exercises.name: Squat Thrust
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a rapid whole-body floor transition without requiring the jump component of later explosive movements.
exercises.description: A rapid floor transition from standing into a supported position and back without the jump component.
setup: Stand with feet comfortably apart.
Clear a safe floor area.
steps: Lower into a squat and place the hands on the floor.
Move the legs back into a straight-arm plank position while keeping the hands planted.
Bring the legs forward and return to standing.
completionCriteria: The player reaches the floor-supported position.
The player returns to standing.

exercises.name: Windshield Wiper
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a substantially more demanding rotational trunk pattern.
exercises.description: A rotational trunk movement in which the legs travel side to side while the upper body remains stable.
setup: Lie on your back with the legs raised together above the body and the shoulders controlled on the floor.
Keep the upper body supported.
steps: Move the legs together toward one side.
Return through center and move toward the other side.
Repeat the side-to-side pattern.
completionCriteria: The legs move together from one side to the other through a controlled side-to-side range.

exercises.name: Star Side Plank
exercises.placementRationale: Extends the side-plank family into a more demanding balance and lateral-stability configuration.
exercises.description: An advanced side-plank position with the top arm and leg extended to increase stability demand.
setup: Set up in a stable side plank.
Arrange the supporting arm and legs before extending the free limbs.
steps: Lift into the side-plank position.
Extend the top arm upward and the top leg away from the body to form the star position.
Maintain the position for the prescribed duration.
keyCues: Do not force the free-limb range.
completionCriteria: The star side-plank position is established with the trunk lifted and the top arm and leg extended.
The prescribed hold duration is completed.

exercises.name: Alternating V-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Adds asymmetrical coordination to the V-Up family.
exercises.description: An alternating V-up pattern performed one side at a time with controlled trunk and hip flexion.
setup: Lie on your back with the limbs extended comfortably.
Prepare to alternate sides.
steps: Raise one leg and the opposite side of the torso until the hand reaches toward the lifted foot or shin.
Lower with control.
Repeat on the opposite side.
completionCriteria: Each alternating repetition reaches the opposite hand-to-foot or shin contact range under control.

exercises.name: Crab Reach
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses from Crab Walk into a more demanding supported rotational movement.
exercises.description: A crab-position transition combining a controlled reach with supported trunk rotation.
setup: Start in a stable crab position with hands and feet supported.
Set the trunk before reaching.
steps: Shift weight into the supporting limbs.
Reach the free arm overhead while rotating the trunk until the shoulder opens toward the ceiling.
Return to the crab position and alternate sides.
completionCriteria: The reaching arm passes overhead while the trunk rotates under control.
The player returns to the starting crab position.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squat Reach
exercises.placementRationale: Combines unilateral squat control with reaching and balance.
exercises.description: A single-leg squat combined with a controlled reach from the lowered position.
setup: Stand tall on one leg.
Use stable support nearby if needed.
steps: Lower into a controlled single-leg squat.
Reach the free hand toward the floor beside the standing foot.
Return to standing with control.
completionCriteria: The single-leg squat reaches the defined controlled depth.
The free hand reaches toward the floor beside the standing foot without losing control.

exercises.name: Reverse Plank
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces sustained posterior-chain and shoulder-extension control from a stable bodyweight position.
exercises.description: A static posterior-chain position performed with the body supported on the hands and feet.
setup: Sit on the floor with your hands behind you and feet planted.
Place the hands so the fingers point comfortably away or slightly outward.
Prepare to lift the hips into a stable reverse-plank position.
steps: Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips.
Extend the body into the controlled reverse-plank position.
Lower with control to return to the starting position.
keyCues: Keep the body long and controlled.
Press firmly through the hands and feet.
completionCriteria: The supported reverse-plank position is established.
The player returns to the starting position.

exercises.name: Plank Walk
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces locomotion while maintaining a high-plank base, increasing shoulder, trunk, and coordination demands.
exercises.description: A traveling plank movement performed while maintaining a controlled trunk position.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position.
Clear enough floor space to move laterally or forward as prescribed.
steps: Move one hand and the opposite or same-side foot in the direction of travel.
Follow with the other limbs while keeping the trunk controlled.
Continue the walking pattern for the prescribed duration.
completionCriteria: The plank-walking pattern is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces substantial asymmetrical loading after staggered and decline push-ups, creating a clear unilateral horizontal-push progression.
exercises.description: An asymmetric push-up in which one arm performs most of the pressing while the other arm remains extended to the side.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position with hands placed wider than a standard push-up.
Keep the body organized in a controlled straight-line position.
steps: Shift your body toward one supporting arm.
Bend the supporting elbow to lower under control while the other arm remains comparatively extended.
Press through the supporting arm to return to the starting position.
Alternate sides as prescribed.
keyCues: Use a controlled range of motion.
completionCriteria: The body lowers under control toward the supporting side.
The player presses back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Prone Elbow Sweep
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a larger controlled scapular and shoulder movement to the established prone pulling family.
exercises.description: A prone upper-back movement that combines elbow drawing with a controlled sweeping motion.
setup: Lie face down with the legs extended comfortably.
Place the arms so they can move freely without striking the floor.
steps: Lift the arms slightly from the floor.
Sweep the elbows outward and backward while drawing the shoulder blades together under control.
Return the arms to the starting position.
keyCues: Move from the upper back and shoulders.
completionCriteria: The arms complete the controlled sweep and return to the starting position.
The arms return under control.

exercises.name: Skater Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a demanding unilateral squat pattern after assisted skater squat and other single-leg control work.
exercises.description: A unilateral squat in which the non-supporting leg stays behind the body in a skater-squat position.
setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg positioned behind you.
Use nearby support when needed for balance and control.
steps: Bend the standing knee and hip to lower the body.
Keep the rear leg off the floor while maintaining balance.
Press through the standing foot to return to upright.
completionCriteria: The player lowers into a controlled single-leg squat while the free leg remains positioned behind the body.
The player returns to upright on the standing leg.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses from stationary and alternating lunge patterns into continuous unilateral locomotion.
exercises.description: A continuous lunge pattern performed while traveling forward.
setup: Stand upright with enough clear space for controlled steps.
steps: Step forward into a lunge.
Lower under control while keeping the trunk organized.
Push through the front foot to continue into the next step.
Alternate legs as you travel.
completionCriteria: Each lunge lowers until the back knee approaches the floor while the front foot remains stable.
The player rises and continues the walking pattern.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squat to Knee Drive
exercises.placementRationale: Combines unilateral squat control with a controlled balance transition after single-leg squat reach work.
exercises.description: A single-leg squat followed by a controlled knee-drive balance transition.
setup: Stand on one leg with the opposite foot free to move.
Use support when needed while learning the movement.
steps: Lower into a controlled single-leg squat.
Drive the free knee upward as you return to standing.
Stabilize briefly before the next repetition.
keyCues: Stand tall before driving the knee.
completionCriteria: The working thigh approaches parallel with the floor during the single-leg squat.
The player returns upright and completes the knee drive with control.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Reach to Knee Drive
exercises.placementRationale: Combines controlled balance, reaching, and return to a stable single-leg position.
exercises.description: A single-leg balance sequence that combines a controlled reach with a return to a knee-drive position.
setup: Stand on one leg with the opposite leg free to move.
Use a stable support nearby if needed.
steps: Reach toward the floor ahead of the standing foot while hinging slightly from the hip.
Return to upright with control.
Drive the free knee upward and stabilize.
completionCriteria: The reach is completed without losing the support position.
The knee drive is completed with controlled balance.

exercises.name: Hollow Rock
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses the static hollow-body position into controlled dynamic rocking.
exercises.description: A controlled rocking movement performed while maintaining a hollow-body trunk position.
setup: Lie on your back on a clear floor.
Set the arms overhead and legs extended while establishing a controlled hollow-body position.
steps: Brace the trunk and lift the shoulders and legs into the hollow position.
Rock gently forward and backward without losing the hollow shape.
Finish by returning to a stable starting position.
completionCriteria: The hollow position is established.
The prescribed rocking repetitions are completed without losing the hollow-body shape.

exercises.name: Plank to Pike
exercises.placementRationale: Adds dynamic trunk and shoulder coordination between high-plank control and later advanced bodyweight skills.
exercises.description: A controlled transition between a high plank and a pike position while maintaining trunk control.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position on the hands and feet.
Clear enough floor space for the full movement.
steps: Press through the hands and lift the hips toward a pike position.
Return under control to the high-plank position.
Repeat without collapsing the trunk.
completionCriteria: The hips rise into a controlled pike position while the hands and feet remain supported.
The player returns to the controlled plank position.

exercises.name: Side Plank Leg Lift
exercises.placementRationale: Increases lateral-stability demand by adding controlled unilateral leg movement to the established side-plank family.
exercises.description: A side-plank variation that adds controlled lifting of the upper leg.
setup: Lie on your side and establish a stable side-plank position.
Stack the legs with the supporting side planted and the top leg ready to lift.
steps: Lift the hips into the side plank.
Raise the upper leg through the controlled range.
Lower the leg and then the hips with control.
keyCues: Move the upper leg without twisting the trunk.
completionCriteria: The side plank is established.
The upper leg lifts away from the lower leg and returns under control without the trunk collapsing.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Mountain Climber
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a more demanding cross-body dynamic trunk pattern after controlled mountain climbers and earlier rotational exercises.
exercises.description: A dynamic mountain-climber movement in which the knee travels toward the opposite side of the body.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position.
Keep enough clearance for alternating leg movement.
steps: Drive one knee toward the opposite side of the torso.
Return the foot and switch sides.
Continue the alternating pattern with controlled trunk position.
completionCriteria: The alternating cross-body pattern is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Lateral Bear Crawl
exercises.placementRationale: Expands bear-crawl movement into lateral whole-body coordination.
exercises.description: A bear crawl performed with controlled lateral travel.
setup: Start in a bear-crawl position with hands under shoulders and knees hovering.
Clear enough floor space for lateral movement.
steps: Move the limbs in a coordinated lateral crawl pattern.
Keep the knees low and the trunk controlled.
Continue traveling for the prescribed duration.
completionCriteria: The lateral bear-crawl pattern continues for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Fast Mountain Climber
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses from controlled and conventional mountain climbers into faster coordinated locomotion.
exercises.description: A faster alternating mountain-climber pattern performed from a stable plank base.
setup: Start in a stable high-plank position.
Clear the floor for rapid alternating leg movement.
steps: Drive one knee forward.
Quickly switch legs while keeping the shoulders supported.
Continue the alternating pattern for the prescribed duration.
keyCues: Move the legs quickly but under control.
completionCriteria: The alternating mountain-climber pattern continues for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Burpee Step
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a full-body floor-to-stand transition without requiring a jump, establishing a progression before later explosive burpee-style movement.
exercises.description: A step-based burpee that removes the jump while retaining the full-body floor transition.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable floor.
Keep enough space to step back and forward safely.
steps: Lower into a squat and place the hands on the floor.
Step the feet back into a plank.
Step the feet forward and return to standing.
completionCriteria: The player completes the floor transition.
The player returns fully to standing.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Calf Raise
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a distinct bent-knee calf pattern rather than simply increasing the difficulty of straight-leg calf raises.
exercises.description: A calf-raise movement performed with the knees slightly bent to emphasize a different ankle-loading position.
setup: Stand with feet comfortably placed and knees slightly bent.
Use a stable support nearby if needed.
steps: Rise onto the balls of the feet.
Pause briefly at the controlled top position.
Lower the heels with control.
completionCriteria: The heels rise to a clear top position while the knees remain slightly bent.
The heels lower under control.

exercises.name: Frog Jump
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a distinct deep-squat-to-jump locomotion pattern after the established jump-squat and other explosive lower-body movements.
exercises.description: A jumping movement from a deep squat-like position with controlled landing.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable surface.
Use enough space for a vertical or slightly forward jump.
steps: Lower into a comfortable squat position.
Jump upward and forward as prescribed.
Land softly with bent knees and regain control.
keyCues: Regain balance before the next repetition.
completionCriteria: The jump is completed.
The landing is controlled and the player regains balance.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces the unsupported pistol squat after assisted pistol and other unilateral control progressions.
exercises.description: A deep single-leg squat with the non-supporting leg held forward.
setup: Stand on one leg with the opposite leg extended forward.
Use a stable support when needed for practice.
steps: Bend the standing knee and hip to lower under control.
Keep the free leg extended forward.
Press through the standing foot to return upright.
keyCues: Use support rather than losing control.
completionCriteria: The player reaches a controlled single-leg squat depth while the free leg remains extended forward.
The player returns to upright.

exercises.name: Assisted Shrimp Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a distinct advanced unilateral squat pattern while retaining assistance.
exercises.description: An assisted shrimp-squat progression using support while performing a deep unilateral squat.
setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg bent behind you.
Hold a stable support within comfortable reach.
steps: Use the support to assist as you lower into the squat.
Keep the rear leg bent and controlled.
Press through the standing foot and use the support only as needed to return upright.
keyCues: Use only as much assistance as needed.
Keep the standing knee aligned with the foot.
completionCriteria: The supported squat reaches a controlled depth with the rear leg bent behind the body.
The player returns to standing with control.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hinge to Knee Drive
exercises.placementRationale: Combines single-leg hinge control with a dynamic return to balance.
exercises.description: A single-leg hinge followed by a controlled return to a knee-drive balance position.
setup: Stand on one leg with the opposite leg free.
Use nearby support if needed.
steps: Hinge forward from the standing hip while the free leg extends behind.
Return to upright with control.
Drive the free knee forward and stabilize.
completionCriteria: The torso and free leg extend backward into a controlled near-straight line during the hinge.
The knee-drive finish is completed with control.

exercises.name: Hollow Rock to Tuck
exercises.placementRationale: Adds controlled shape change to the hollow-rock progression rather than simply increasing duration.
exercises.description: A controlled transition from a hollow rocking position into a compact tuck and back.
setup: Lie on your back on a clear floor.
Establish a hollow-body position with the arms overhead and legs extended.
steps: Rock from the hollow position with control.
Draw the knees inward into the tuck position.
Extend back to the hollow position without losing trunk control.
completionCriteria: The hollow-to-tuck transition is completed.
The player returns to the hollow position under control.

exercises.name: Side Plank Thread the Needle
exercises.placementRationale: Combines lateral stability with controlled trunk rotation.
exercises.description: A side-plank movement that adds controlled trunk rotation and arm threading.
setup: Establish a stable side-plank position.
Place the upper arm where it can move freely.
steps: Reach the upper arm toward the ceiling with the chest open.
Rotate the trunk and thread the upper arm under the torso until the shoulder rotates comfortably.
Return to the starting side-plank position.
completionCriteria: The upper arm passes underneath the torso while the trunk rotates under control.
The player returns to the side-plank position.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces stronger lateral propulsion and single-leg landing control after Skater Step and Skater Jump.
exercises.description: A powerful lateral jump from one leg to the other with controlled landing.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable surface.
Use enough lateral space for controlled jumps.
steps: Load the takeoff leg.
Push laterally and travel to the opposite side.
Land on the opposite leg and stabilize.
Repeat to the other side as prescribed.
completionCriteria: The lateral jump is completed.
The landing is controlled on the receiving leg.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces horizontal jumping and landing control as a distinct explosive movement capability.
exercises.description: A horizontal jump that emphasizes coordinated takeoff and controlled landing.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable surface with space ahead.
steps: Bend at the hips and knees to load the legs.
Swing the arms and jump forward.
Land with bent knees and regain balance.
completionCriteria: The player completes the forward jump.
The landing is controlled before resetting.

exercises.name: Tuck Jump
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a more coordinated explosive squat pattern after the established jump squat.
exercises.description: An explosive jump that brings the knees upward during flight.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable surface.
Use enough overhead and floor clearance for the movement.
steps: Lower into a controlled preparatory squat.
Jump upward and bring the knees upward during flight.
Land softly with bent knees and regain control.
keyCues: Bring the knees up without losing body control.
completionCriteria: The jump and knee-tuck action are completed.
The landing is controlled.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bent-Knee Calf Raise
exercises.placementRationale: Combines unilateral loading with the newer bent-knee calf pattern.
exercises.description: A single-leg calf raise performed with a softly bent knee.
setup: Stand on one leg with the opposite foot clear of the floor.
Use stable support nearby if needed.
Keep the standing knee slightly bent.
steps: Rise onto the ball of the standing foot.
Lower the heel with control.
Repeat while maintaining the bent-knee position.
completionCriteria: The heel rises to a clear top position while the standing knee remains softly bent.
The heel lowers under control.

exercises.name: Sliding Hamstring Curl
setupRequirements: stable low-friction sliding surface or appropriate sliders
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a substantially more demanding hamstring-dominant movement using controlled sliding resistance.
exercises.description: A hamstring-focused curl performed using a sliding surface for added resistance.
setup: Use a stable low-friction surface or sliders.
Lie down and set the heels on the sliding surface.
Prepare the body in a controlled bridge or curl start position.
steps: Pull the heels toward the body under control.
Keep the hamstrings engaged through the curl.
Extend back out to the starting position.
keyCues: Use the hamstrings rather than momentum.
completionCriteria: The heels draw toward the body while the hips remain lifted and controlled.
The legs extend back to the starting bridge position with control.

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a higher-skill unilateral squat after assisted shrimp and pistol-squat progression has been established.
exercises.description: A deep unilateral squat in the shrimp-squat position without external support.
setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg bent behind you.
Use a clear floor and stable surface.
steps: Lower into the shrimp-squat position with control.
Keep the rear leg bent and the trunk organized.
Press through the standing foot to return upright.
keyCues: Use a smooth return to standing.
completionCriteria: The player reaches a controlled shrimp-squat position with the rear leg bent and the working foot stable.
The player returns upright under control.

exercises.name: Star Side Plank Reach
exercises.placementRationale: Builds on Star Side Plank with additional controlled upper-body movement.
exercises.description: A star side plank that adds a controlled reaching action while maintaining lateral trunk stability.
setup: Establish a stable side-plank position.
Position the free arm upward and the upper leg extended away from the body to prepare the star shape.
steps: Lift into the star side-plank position.
Reach the free arm upward and away from the body while maintaining the star side-plank position.
Return to the starting position with control.
keyCues: Reach without collapsing the supporting side.
completionCriteria: The star position is established.
The reach is completed and the player returns under control.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.placementRationale: Builds on the Tier 4A step-burpee pattern by adding the full floor-to-stand sequence.
exercises.description: A full-body floor transition that combines a squat, plank position, return, and controlled jump.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable surface.
Ensure enough space for the full floor transition and jump.
steps: Lower into a squat and place the hands on the floor.
Move the feet back into a plank.
Return the feet toward the hands and rise.
Perform the programmed jump and land under control with the knees bent.
completionCriteria: The floor transition is completed.
The player returns upright and completes the jump with a controlled landing.

exercises.name: Diagonal Bear Crawl
exercises.placementRationale: Adds diagonal whole-body crawling coordination beyond forward and lateral bear-crawl patterns.
exercises.description: A bear crawl performed with controlled diagonal travel and coordinated limb movement.
setup: Start in a bear-crawl position.
Clear enough floor space for diagonal travel.
steps: Move the limbs in a coordinated diagonal crawling pattern.
Keep the knees hovering low to the floor.
Continue traveling diagonally for the prescribed duration.
completionCriteria: The diagonal bear-crawl pattern continues for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Split Jump
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces repeated vertical propulsion from a split stance after non-impact lunge progressions.
exercises.description: An explosive jumping movement that switches the legs between split positions in the air.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable surface.
Use enough space for repeated jumping and safe landings.
steps: Lower into a split stance with control.
Jump upward and switch the leg positions during flight.
Land softly and prepare for the next repetition.
completionCriteria: The split position is changed during the jump.
The landing is controlled before the next repetition.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
setupRequirements: secure horizontal bar or equivalent stable pulling setup that allows the body to pull toward the support
exercises.placementRationale: Adds the missing bodyweight horizontal-pulling strength bridge between prone scapular-control work and the later front-lever pathway.
exercises.description: A bodyweight horizontal pulling movement in which the chest is pulled toward a stable horizontal support while the body remains braced.
setup: Use a secure horizontal bar or equivalent stable support set at a suitable height.
Position the body underneath the support with the hands gripping the bar and the body held in a straight line.
Set the shoulders and brace the trunk before pulling.
steps: Pull the chest toward the support while keeping the body aligned.
Bring the chest toward the bar without shrugging or swinging.
Lower the body under control until the arms are straight again.
keyCues: Drive the elbows back toward the body.
Avoid swinging or collapsing through the shoulders.
completionCriteria: The chest reaches the defined pulling position close to the support.
The player returns to the straight-body starting position with control.

exercises.name: Burpee Jump
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a controlled jump to the established Burpee after the earlier step-based floor transition.
exercises.description: A burpee variation that finishes with a controlled jump after the floor transition.
setup: Stand on a clear, stable surface.
Make sure you have enough room to lower to the floor and rise again.
Set yourself into the starting stance.
steps: Lower into a squat and place your hands on the floor.
Move through the burpee floor transition with control.
Return to standing and finish with a controlled jump.
Land softly and regain balance.
completionCriteria: The floor transition is completed.
The jump is completed with a controlled landing.

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic
exercises.placementRationale: Grouped as a knee-extension/quadriceps capability rather than a squat pattern; the kneeling bodyweight movement directly develops controlled knee-extension strength.
exercises.description: A kneeling quadriceps-focused movement that leans back and returns under control.
setup: Use a padded floor or kneeling surface.
Set both knees in a comfortable kneeling position.
Keep the torso tall at the start.
steps: Lean backward from the knees under control.
Keep the hips extended as you move.
Return to the starting kneeling position.
completionCriteria: The backward lean is completed.
The player returns to the starting kneeling position.
readinessRequirements: controlled kneeling bodyweight technique and ability to manage the extended-knee loading position

exercises.name: Hip Airplane
exercises.placementRationale: Combines single-leg balance, controlled hip rotation, and hinge control into a substantially more demanding movement.
exercises.description: A single-leg balance movement that combines hinging with controlled hip rotation.
setup: Stand on one leg.
Keep the other leg lightly extended behind you.
Make sure you have clear space to rotate safely.
steps: Hinge forward from the hip while staying balanced.
Open and close the hips under control.
Return to the starting balance position.
completionCriteria: Single-leg balance is maintained through the controlled hip hinge and hip-rotation pattern.
The rotation is completed under control.

exercises.name: Pogo Hop
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces repetitive elastic ankle movement after the non-impact calf and jump foundations established in earlier tiers.
exercises.description: A quick elastic ankle hop performed with minimal knee bend.
setup: Stand on a clear surface.
Set your feet close and ready to spring.
Prepare for small, quick hops.
steps: Perform small, repeated hops from the ankles.
Keep the body tall and springy.
Land quietly and continue the rhythm.
keyCues: Use the ankles, not a deep knee bend.
Keep the hops quick and controlled.
completionCriteria: The repeated low-amplitude ankle-driven hops are maintained with controlled landings.
The player lands with control.
readinessRequirements: controlled low-impact landing mechanics and ankle stiffness control

exercises.name: Long-Lever Plank
exercises.placementRationale: Increases trunk-control demand through a substantially less favorable leverage position than the standard plank family.
exercises.description: A plank held with the body positioned farther from the hands to increase lever demand.
setup: Set up on a clear floor surface.
Place the hands in a longer reach than a standard plank.
Align the body for a stable plank line.
steps: Lift into the long-lever plank.
Maintain the body line without sagging.
Return to the starting position with control.
keyCues: Do not let the hips drop.
completionCriteria: The long-lever plank position is maintained for the prescribed duration without losing trunk control.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl Kick-Through
exercises.placementRationale: Combines crawling locomotion with controlled rotation and limb coordination.
exercises.description: A crawling locomotion pattern that adds a controlled rotational kick-through.
setup: Use a clear floor space.
Start in a bear crawl position.
Make sure there is room to rotate the leg through safely.
steps: Move in the bear crawl pattern.
Rotate one leg through under control.
Return to the bear base and continue on the other side.
completionCriteria: The crawl and kick-through pattern is completed.

exercises.name: Wall Walk
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a substantially more demanding shoulder and whole-body coordination skill after the pike-push-up progression.
exercises.description: A wall-based inversion transition that walks the body toward and away from the wall.
setup: Use a clear wall and floor.
Make sure your hands can stay on a stable surface.
Set up with enough room for the full transition.
steps: Start in a plank facing the wall.
Walk the feet up and move the hands closer to the wall under control.
Reverse the motion to return to the starting position.
keyCues: Use the wall as a stable guide.
completionCriteria: The wall walk transition is completed.

exercises.name: Clap Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces explosive horizontal pushing only after substantial conventional and asymmetric push-up development.
exercises.description: An explosive push-up that leaves the floor with a controlled clap before landing.
setup: Use a clear floor space.
Set up in a strong push-up position.
Make sure the landing space is unobstructed.
steps: Lower into a controlled push-up.
Press forcefully enough to leave the floor.
Clap under control and land back in the push-up position.
keyCues: Land softly and regain the base position.
completionCriteria: The clap is completed.
The player returns to the push-up base position with control.
readinessRequirements: controlled push-up technique and ability to land the hands softly and stably

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
setupRequirements: secure pull-up bar or equivalent stable vertical pulling setup
exercises.placementRationale: Provides an earlier vertical-pull foundation through controlled scapular movement before the later assisted full-range pull-up.
exercises.description: A hanging vertical-pull foundation in which the player moves primarily through controlled scapular motion before full-range pulling.
setup: Grip a secure pull-up bar or equivalent overhead support.
Hang with the body in a controlled position appropriate to the setup.
Allow the shoulders to settle into the starting position.
steps: Depress and retract the shoulder blades to raise the body slightly without a full elbow-driven pull.
Return to the starting scapular position with control.
Repeat the scapular movement without swinging.
keyCues: Move from the shoulders rather than swinging the legs.
completionCriteria: The shoulders depress and the body rises slightly while the elbows remain nearly straight.
The player returns to the starting hanging position under control.
readinessRequirements: secure overhead support and controlled hanging technique

exercises.name: Assisted One-Arm Incline Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a true unilateral horizontal-push pathway while retaining an elevated setup for controlled progression.
exercises.description: A unilateral incline push-up with one side receiving assistance from the raised surface.
setup: Use a stable incline such as a bench or box.
Set one hand on the incline and the other in the assisted position.
Make sure the setup feels stable before starting.
steps: Lower through the incline push-up pattern with control.
Keep the working side engaged while the assisted side supports the movement.
Press back to the starting position.
keyCues: Use the incline for controlled support.
completionCriteria: The lowering and pressing phases are both completed.
The player returns to the starting position.
readinessRequirements: controlled asymmetric push-up technique and a stable elevated support

exercises.name: Planche Lean
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces planche-style forward-lever loading as a controlled preparatory skill before later planche-oriented pressing.
exercises.description: A forward-leaning push support that prepares the body for later planche-oriented work.
setup: Use a clear floor surface.
Place the hands firmly on the floor.
Lean the shoulders forward while keeping the elbows controlled.
steps: Shift into the forward-leaning support position.
Maintain the lean without collapsing the shoulders.
Return to the starting position with control.
keyCues: Keep the shoulders protracted and engaged.
Stay smooth through the wrists and trunk.
completionCriteria: The shoulders shift forward past the hands while the feet remain supported and the body stays controlled.
The player returns to the start with control.
readinessRequirements: controlled push-up support and ability to maintain a stable forward-leaning shoulder position

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hop to Stick
exercises.placementRationale: Adds single-leg propulsion followed by controlled landing and stabilization.
exercises.description: A single-leg hop that finishes with a controlled landing and stabilization.
setup: Stand on one leg with enough clear landing space.
Prepare to hop forward or in place under control.
Set the eyes on a stable landing target.
steps: Perform a single-leg hop.
Land on the same leg with control.
Hold the landing without wobbling.
completionCriteria: The hop is completed.
The landing is stabilized under control.

exercises.name: Side Plank Knee Tuck
exercises.placementRationale: Combines lateral trunk stability with controlled lower-limb movement.
exercises.description: A side-plank variation that adds a controlled knee tuck.
setup: Start in a stable side-plank setup.
Keep the supporting shoulder ready to bear load.
Prepare the free leg to tuck under control.
steps: Lift into the side plank.
Draw the top knee in toward the torso.
Return to the start position and repeat on the opposite side when the workout prescription calls for alternating sides.
keyCues: Move the knee without collapsing the hip.
Stay controlled through the side body.
completionCriteria: The side plank base is maintained.
The knee tuck is completed with control.

exercises.name: Alternating Bound
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces repeated unilateral horizontal propulsion after earlier jumping and lateral-bound foundations.
exercises.description: A repeated unilateral bound pattern that moves from side to side or forward with rhythm.
setup: Use a clear floor space.
Stand ready to propel from one leg at a time.
Make sure the landing area is free of obstacles.
steps: Bound off one leg.
Land under control on the opposite side or next contact point.
Continue alternating with a steady rhythm.
keyCues: Push off forcefully but under control.
Keep the rhythm smooth and repeatable.
completionCriteria: The required alternating bounds are completed with controlled takeoffs and landings.
readinessRequirements: controlled single-leg landing mechanics and ability to decelerate each landing

exercises.name: Single-Leg Pogo Hop
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses the bilateral elastic ankle pattern into unilateral repetitive hopping.
exercises.description: A unilateral elastic ankle hop performed with minimal ground contact time.
setup: Stand on one leg on a clear surface.
Keep the free leg quiet and ready.
Prepare to hop lightly from the ankle.
steps: Perform small quick hops on one leg.
Keep the body tall and springy.
Land quietly and continue the rhythm.
keyCues: Use the ankle, not a deep squat.
Keep the hop cycle quick and controlled.
completionCriteria: The unilateral pogo pattern is completed with control.
readinessRequirements: controlled single-leg landing mechanics and ankle stability

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bound to Stick
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses single-leg hopping into larger horizontal propulsion followed by controlled stabilization.
exercises.description: A larger single-leg bound that finishes with a controlled landing and hold.
setup: Stand on one leg with clear landing space.
Set a target for the bound and stick.
Prepare to propel and stabilize.
steps: Bound off one leg.
Land on the target leg with control.
Hold the landing until stable.
completionCriteria: The bound is completed.
The landing is stabilized under control.
readinessRequirements: controlled single-leg landing and balance after horizontal propulsion

exercises.name: Pseudo-Planche Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Builds directly on the Tier 5 Planche Lean and introduces dynamic pressing under substantially altered horizontal-push leverage.
exercises.description: A horizontal push-up variation performed with the shoulders shifted forward of the hands to increase the leverage demand on the upper body and trunk.
setup: Place your hands on a stable floor or appropriate hand supports.
Extend your legs behind you and establish a stable push-up position.
Shift your shoulders forward relative to your hands while keeping the body controlled.
steps: Maintain the forward-leaning push-up position as you lower your body.
Press through your hands to return to the starting position.
Reset the body position before the next repetition.
keyCues: Keep the body controlled as one unit.
Use a controlled range of motion.
completionCriteria: The chest lowers toward the floor while the shoulders remain forward of the hands.
The player returns to the forward-leaning starting position with control.
readinessRequirements: controlled advanced push-up technique and ability to maintain the forward shoulder lean

exercises.name: Assisted Nordic Hamstring Curl
setupRequirements: secure lower-leg anchoring or equivalent stable setup
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a high-demand hamstring knee-flexion movement with assistance before the full Nordic curl.
exercises.description: A kneeling hamstring curl performed with assistance so the player can control the lowering and return with reduced loading.
setup: Secure the lower legs against a stable anchor or equivalent setup.
Kneel upright with the body aligned from knees through the trunk.
Arrange the assistance method so it can support a controlled return.
steps: Brace the trunk and begin lowering the body forward from the knees.
Control the descent until the torso approaches the floor without losing the straight-body line.
Use the configured assistance to return to the upright kneeling position.
keyCues: Use assistance deliberately for the return.
completionCriteria: The torso approaches the floor under control while the body remains aligned.
The player returns to the upright kneeling start position.
readinessRequirements: controlled kneeling hamstring loading and appropriate assistance setup

exercises.name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop to Stick
exercises.placementRationale: Adds lateral single-leg propulsion and stabilization beyond the earlier linear hop-to-stick progression.
exercises.description: A lateral single-leg hop followed by a controlled landing and stabilization on one leg.
setup: Stand with enough clear floor space for a controlled lateral hop.
Choose a stable starting stance and focus on the landing area.
steps: Hop laterally from the starting leg.
Land on the opposite leg and stabilize.
Regain a controlled single-leg position before the next repetition.
keyCues: Keep the standing knee and foot aligned comfortably.
completionCriteria: The lateral hop is completed.
The landing is stabilized on one leg before the repetition is counted.

exercises.name: Long-Lever Side Plank
exercises.placementRationale: Increases lateral trunk leverage demands beyond the standard and dynamic side-plank family.
exercises.description: A side plank performed with a longer body lever to increase the lateral trunk-stability demand.
setup: Lie on your side with the supporting forearm or hand positioned securely.
Straighten both legs with the feet stacked and align the body before lifting.
steps: Lift the hips to establish the long-lever side plank.
Maintain the position for the prescribed hold duration.
Lower with control after completing the hold.
keyCues: Avoid rotating or sagging through the hips.
completionCriteria: The body forms a straight line from head through feet in the long-lever side plank.
The prescribed hold duration is completed while maintaining that position.

exercises.name: Tuck L-Sit Support
setupRequirements: stable hand supports such as parallel bars, sturdy blocks, or equivalent equipment
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces supported L-sit mechanics as a distinct high-level trunk-compression and shoulder-support capability before the full L-sit.
exercises.description: A supported seated compression position with the knees drawn toward the trunk and the body held from stable hand supports.
setup: Place your hands on stable supports beside the body.
Position your body between or just behind the supports with the feet on the floor initially.
Prepare to lift the body while keeping the knees bent.
steps: Press down through the supports to lift the body.
Draw the knees toward the trunk and hold the supported tuck position.
Lower back to the starting position with control.
completionCriteria: The body is lifted clear of the starting support position.
The knees remain tucked while the supported hold is maintained for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Lateral Pogo Hop
exercises.placementRationale: Extends the bilateral vertical pogo pattern into controlled lateral elastic ankle movement.
exercises.description: A repeated lateral pogo pattern emphasizing elastic ankle action and controlled side-to-side landings.
setup: Stand with clear space to move laterally.
Adopt a comfortable athletic stance.
steps: Perform a quick lateral hop driven primarily through the feet and ankles.
Land under control and rebound laterally.
Continue the repeated lateral pattern for the prescribed repetitions.
keyCues: Keep the contacts light and controlled.
Use the ankles and feet to manage the rebound.
completionCriteria: Each prescribed lateral hop is completed.
The player maintains control through the landing and rebound sequence.
readinessRequirements: controlled landing mechanics and side-to-side ankle control

exercises.name: Typewriter Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces controlled side-to-side weight transfer through the push-up position, extending the unilateral-loading pathway beyond Archer Push-Up.
exercises.description: A push-up variation in which the body shifts laterally across the hands, increasing asymmetric loading and control demands.
setup: Start in a stable push-up position with the hands wider than shoulder width to allow controlled side-to-side shifting.
steps: Lower into the push-up position.
Shift the body toward one hand while keeping the other arm more extended.
Return through the center and repeat toward the opposite side.
completionCriteria: The player completes the push-up movement with the trunk controlled.
A controlled lateral shift is completed toward each side with the opposite arm extending more fully.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
setupRequirements: secure lower-leg anchoring or equivalent stable setup
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses directly from the assisted Nordic version to the full bodyweight knee-flexion movement.
exercises.description: A full bodyweight Nordic hamstring curl performed from a kneeling position with controlled lowering and return.
setup: Secure the lower legs against a stable anchor or equivalent setup.
Kneel upright with the trunk controlled.
steps: Brace the trunk and begin leaning forward from the knees.
Control the lowering phase until the torso approaches the floor while keeping the hips and trunk aligned.
Use an appropriate assisted return to the upright kneeling position.
keyCues: Keep the trunk rigid and controlled.
completionCriteria: The body lowers toward the floor under control while maintaining a straight line from knees through shoulders.
The player returns to the starting kneeling position.
readinessRequirements: controlled hamstring loading and secure lower-leg anchoring

exercises.name: Body Saw
setupRequirements: smooth controlled sliding surface or appropriate sliders
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces dynamic long-lever anti-extension work using a distinct sliding mechanism rather than another static plank variation.
exercises.description: A dynamic anti-extension exercise performed from a forearm-plank position by moving the body as a controlled unit through a sliding motion.
setup: Place the forearms on a stable surface or use appropriate sliders.
Extend the legs behind you and establish a controlled forearm-plank position.
Set the body into a stable starting alignment.
steps: Slide or glide the body backward while maintaining trunk position.
Return toward the starting position without allowing the lower back to arch excessively.
Repeat the controlled sliding movement.
keyCues: Move the body as one unit.
Use a controlled range rather than a fast rocking motion.
completionCriteria: The body slides forward and backward through a controlled range while the plank position is maintained.
The starting trunk position is regained under control.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bound
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses from alternating bounds and controlled bound-to-stick work into continuous unilateral horizontal propulsion.
exercises.description: A repeated single-leg horizontal propulsion movement in which each bound is followed by a controlled transition to the next bound.
setup: Stand in a clear area suitable for horizontal movement.
Adopt a balanced single-leg starting position.
steps: Drive forward from one leg into a controlled bound.
Land on the opposite leg and transition into the next bound.
Continue the alternating propulsion pattern for the prescribed repetitions.
keyCues: Project the body forward under control.
Use the landing to prepare the next bound.
completionCriteria: Each prescribed bound is completed.
The player maintains control through each landing and transition.
readinessRequirements: controlled single-leg landing mechanics and ability to decelerate from horizontal propulsion

exercises.name: Single-Leg Lateral Pogo Hop
exercises.placementRationale: Adds unilateral loading to the established lateral pogo movement.
exercises.description: A repeated lateral pogo hop performed on one leg, emphasizing elastic ankle control and balance.
setup: Stand in a clear area with enough lateral space.
Begin balanced on one leg with the supporting foot stable.
steps: Perform a short lateral pogo hop from the supporting foot.
Land on the same foot and rebound laterally with control.
Complete the prescribed repetitions on one side, then switch sides.
keyCues: Keep the hops controlled and compact.
completionCriteria: Each prescribed hop is completed on the supporting leg.
The player retains balance through the landing and rebound.
readinessRequirements: controlled single-leg landing mechanics and lateral ankle stability

exercises.name: One-Arm Push-Up
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces the full unilateral horizontal-push movement after the Tier 5 assisted incline pathway and Tier 6 asymmetrical work.
exercises.description: A unilateral horizontal push-up performed primarily through one arm while the body remains controlled throughout the movement.
setup: Place the working hand beneath the working shoulder and position the non-working arm away from the floor so it cannot assist.
steps: Lower the body toward the working arm under control.
Press through the working arm to return to the starting position.
Reset the body before the next repetition and perform the opposite side when the workout prescription calls for alternating sides.
keyCues: Use a manageable range of motion with deliberate control.
completionCriteria: The chest lowers toward the floor while the body remains controlled over the working arm.
The player returns to the starting position using the working arm.
readinessRequirements: strong controlled push-up technique and the ability to maintain a stable unilateral support position

exercises.name: L-Sit
setupRequirements: stable hand supports such as parallel bars, sturdy blocks, or equivalent equipment
exercises.placementRationale: Completes the progression from supported tuck L-sit mechanics to the full L-sit position.
exercises.description: An unsupported L-sit compression position in which the body is held from stable hand supports with the legs extended forward.
setup: Place your hands on stable supports beside or slightly ahead of the hips.
Extend the shoulders into a strong support position.
Prepare to lift the body with both legs together and straight in front.
steps: Press down through the supports to lift the hips from the surface.
Extend the legs forward into the L-sit position.
Maintain the position for the prescribed hold duration, then lower with control.
keyCues: Maintain a steady trunk and avoid swinging.
completionCriteria: The hips are lifted clear of the support surface.
Both legs remain together and straight in front for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Burpee Broad Jump
exercises.placementRationale: Combines the established Burpee and Broad Jump patterns into a distinct whole-body propulsion movement.
exercises.description: A full-body floor transition followed by a controlled broad jump, combining rapid movement between positions with horizontal propulsion.
setup: Stand with clear floor space in front of you.
Use a landing area that allows the jump to be controlled.
steps: Lower into the burpee floor transition.
Return to standing with control.
Jump forward into a broad jump and land under control.
Reset to the starting stance before the next repetition.
keyCues: Move through the transition under control.
Use only the jump distance that can be controlled.
completionCriteria: The floor transition is completed.
The broad jump and landing are completed with control.
The player returns to the starting stance before the next repetition.
readinessRequirements: controlled burpee technique and controlled landing mechanics for the broad jump

exercises.name: Single-Leg Lateral Bound to Stick
exercises.placementRationale: Builds on lateral hop and bound work with greater unilateral propulsion followed by controlled stabilization.
exercises.description: A larger lateral single-leg bound followed by a deliberate one-leg landing and stabilization.
setup: Stand in a clear area with enough lateral room for the bound.
Begin balanced on one leg with the landing area in view.
steps: Drive laterally into a bound from the starting leg.
Land on the opposite leg and stabilize the body.
Hold the landing long enough to establish control before the next repetition.
completionCriteria: The lateral bound is completed.
The landing is stabilized on one leg before the repetition is counted.
readinessRequirements: controlled lateral single-leg landing and balance

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up
setupRequirements: secure pull-up bar or equivalent stable vertical pulling setup
exercises.placementRationale: Provides a controlled full-range vertical-pull bridge after the earlier Scapular Pull-Up foundation and before the unassisted Pull-Up.
readinessRequirements: appropriate assistance, secure overhead support, and controlled hanging/pulling technique
exercises.description: A full-range vertical pulling movement performed with assistance sufficient to support controlled technique.
setup: Use a secure pull-up bar or equivalent vertical pulling setup.
Set the appropriate assistance before beginning.
Start from a controlled hang with the arms extended and shoulders set.
steps: Pull the body upward while maintaining the selected assistance.
Continue until the chin reaches bar height.
Lower back to the controlled hanging start position.
completionCriteria: The chin reaches bar height with the body under control.
The body returns to the starting hang with control.

exercises.name: Wall-Supported Handstand Hold
setupRequirements: stable wall-supported setup
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces controlled inversion and overhead body positioning after the Tier 6 pike and advanced pressing pathway without requiring freestanding balance.
readinessRequirements: advanced inverted skill requiring qualified supervision and appropriate technique readiness
exercises.description: A wall-supported inverted hold that develops overhead strength, body positioning, and controlled inversion.
setup: Use a stable wall with clear space around you.
Set the hands on a stable floor surface at an appropriate distance from the wall.
Establish a controlled wall-supported inverted position.
steps: Move into the wall-supported handstand position with control.
Establish a wall-supported handstand with the arms straight and the body inverted in a controlled position.
Hold for the prescribed duration, then exit the inversion under control.
keyCues: Do not rush the entry or exit.
completionCriteria: The wall-supported inverted position is established with control.
The prescribed hold duration is completed while maintaining the controlled position.

exercises.name: Tuck Planche Hold
setupRequirements: stable floor or hand supports
exercises.placementRationale: Creates the static skill bridge between Tier 5 Planche Lean and Tier 6 Pseudo-Planche Push-Up before later dynamic planche pressing.
exercises.description: A static planche skill in which the body is supported by the hands while the knees remain tucked toward the trunk.
setup: Use a stable floor or appropriate hand supports.
Place the hands securely and lean the shoulders forward over the hands.
Tuck both knees toward the chest and prepare to lift the feet.
steps: Shift the shoulders forward over the hands while maintaining control.
Lift the body into the tucked planche position.
Hold for the prescribed duration, then lower with control.
keyCues: Maintain the tuck without losing body control.
completionCriteria: The feet remain off the ground while the shoulders stay forward of the hands and the knees remain tucked.
The prescribed hold duration is completed without losing the tuck planche shape.
readinessRequirements: substantial prior pushing, shoulder-support, and body-tension control

exercises.name: V-Sit
exercises.placementRationale: Advances the Tier 6 L-Sit compression pathway by requiring a substantially greater combination of active compression, balance, and trunk control.
exercises.description: An advanced compression position with the torso upright and the legs extended upward in front of the body.
setup: Begin seated on a stable floor surface.
Place the hands beside the hips in a position that allows controlled support.
Prepare the trunk and legs for an active compression position.
steps: Press through the hands to establish controlled support.
Lift the legs into the V-sit position while maintaining active trunk control.
Hold for the prescribed duration, then lower with control.
completionCriteria: The V-sit position is established under control.
The prescribed hold duration is completed while maintaining the position.

exercises.name: Handstand Push-Up
setupRequirements: stable wall-supported setup
exercises.placementRationale: Extends the supported handstand position into advanced vertical pressing strength after substantial pike and shoulder-development work.
readinessRequirements: advanced inverted skill requiring qualified supervision and appropriate technique readiness
exercises.description: An advanced inverted pressing movement performed from a controlled wall-supported handstand position.
setup: Use a stable wall-supported handstand setup with clear space around you.
Place the hands securely and establish the starting inverted position.
Use an appropriate setup that allows controlled entry and exit.
steps: Lower the head and shoulders toward the floor through a controlled pressing range while maintaining the wall-supported inverted position.
Press through the hands to return to the starting position.
Exit the inverted position with control after the repetition or set.
keyCues: Use a deliberate range of motion.
completionCriteria: The head and shoulders are lowered toward the floor and the body is pressed back to the supported handstand position under control.
The player returns to the supported handstand position.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Nordic Hamstring Curl
setupRequirements: secure lower-leg anchoring or equivalent stable setup
exercises.placementRationale: Extends the Tier 6 full Nordic pathway into a substantially more unilateral hamstring knee-flexion demand.
exercises.description: A highly demanding unilateral Nordic hamstring curl using one working leg to control the movement.
setup: Secure the lower leg against a stable anchor or equivalent setup.
Kneel upright with the working leg positioned for a controlled Nordic movement.
Use a setup that permits a controlled range and stable return.
steps: Brace the trunk and begin lowering forward from one working knee.
Control the descent until the torso approaches the floor while the working leg remains the primary support.
Use an appropriate assisted return to the upright position.
keyCues: Maintain the working-leg position throughout the movement.
completionCriteria: The unilateral lowering phase approaches the floor under control without losing body alignment.
The player returns to the upright starting position with control.
readinessRequirements: substantial prior hamstring control and secure lower-leg anchoring

exercises.name: Dragon Flag
setupRequirements: stable support capable of handling the required body position
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a very demanding long-lever anti-extension skill after Hollow, Body Saw, and L-Sit development.
exercises.description: A highly demanding long-lever trunk exercise in which the body is controlled as a rigid unit from a supported upper-body position.
setup: Use a stable bench or support with a secure upper-body handhold.
Lie on your back with the shoulders anchored to the support and the body extended.
Brace the trunk before lifting the hips.
steps: Lift the body as a single rigid unit from the support.
Lower the body slowly toward the support while maintaining the straight-body lever.
Return to the starting position without losing whole-body control.
keyCues: Keep the body rigid and controlled.
Do not drop or swing through the movement.
completionCriteria: The body lowers toward the support as one controlled unit without the hips folding.
The player returns to the anchored starting position without losing the rigid body line.
readinessRequirements: advanced trunk-control technique and a secure support capable of anchoring the upper body

exercises.name: Tuck Planche Push-Up
setupRequirements: stable floor or hand supports
exercises.placementRationale: Adds dynamic pressing to the Tuck Planche Hold and Pseudo-Planche Push-Up pathway as an advanced planche-pressing skill.
exercises.description: A dynamic pressing movement performed from a controlled tuck planche position.
setup: Use a stable floor or appropriate hand supports.
Place the hands securely and establish a controlled tuck planche starting position.
Ensure the surrounding area is clear.
steps: Lower the body from the tuck planche position by bending the elbows while keeping the knees tucked and feet elevated.
Press back to the tuck planche starting position with control.
Reset the body position before the next repetition.
keyCues: Use a controlled range rather than forcing depth.
completionCriteria: The elbows bend clearly while the tuck planche shape remains intact.
The player returns to the starting tuck planche position with control.
readinessRequirements: substantial tuck-planche support control and advanced pushing technique

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
setupRequirements: secure pull-up bar or equivalent stable hanging setup
exercises.placementRationale: Adds a hanging compression pattern that combines trunk control, shoulder support, and active hip flexion beyond the floor-based L-Sit pathway.
readinessRequirements: appropriate hanging and trunk-control readiness
exercises.description: A hanging compression movement in which the legs are actively raised while the body remains controlled from an overhead support.
setup: Use a secure pull-up bar or equivalent hanging setup.
Establish a stable hanging position.
Clear the surrounding area before beginning.
steps: Brace the trunk and raise the straight legs until they are approximately parallel to the floor.
Control the legs at the top of the movement.
Lower the legs back to the controlled hanging start without excessive swinging.
keyCues: Raise the legs with active trunk control.
completionCriteria: The straight legs reach approximately parallel to the floor under control.
The legs return to the controlled hanging start without excessive swinging.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
setupRequirements: secure pull-up bar or equivalent stable vertical pulling setup
exercises.placementRationale: Progresses from assisted vertical pulling to an unassisted bodyweight pull-up.
exercises.description: A standard unassisted vertical pulling movement performed from a secure hanging setup.
setup: Use a secure pull-up bar or equivalent vertical pulling setup.
Begin from a controlled hang with the arms extended and the body stable beneath the bar.
Establish a controlled starting grip.
steps: Pull the body upward until the chin clears the bar.
Lower back to the starting hang without excessive swinging.
keyCues: Use a consistent range of motion.
completionCriteria: The chin clears the bar with the body under control.
The body returns to the starting hang with control.
readinessRequirements: controlled hanging technique and the ability to maintain a stable body during an unassisted pull

exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever
setupRequirements: secure horizontal or pull-up bar setup capable of supporting the body
exercises.placementRationale: Introduces a major advanced pulling-lever skill built around full-body horizontal tension and controlled scapular positioning.
readinessRequirements: advanced pulling and body-tension skill readiness
exercises.description: An advanced horizontal pulling skill that holds the body in a tucked lever position using full-body tension and scapular control.
setup: Use a secure horizontal bar or equivalent support capable of supporting the body.
Start hanging with the arms extended and shoulders controlled.
Draw both knees toward the chest before establishing the lever.
steps: Pull the body into the tucked lever position.
Maintain the tucked body shape and controlled scapular position.
Hold for the prescribed duration, then return to the starting position with control.
keyCues: Maintain the tuck throughout the hold.
Keep the support stable and avoid swinging.
completionCriteria: The body is held in a stable tucked horizontal lever with the hips lifted to the lever line.
The prescribed hold duration is completed without losing the tuck or swinging.

exercises.name: Archer Pull-Up
setupRequirements: secure pull-up bar or equivalent stable vertical pulling setup
exercises.placementRationale: Raises the unilateral loading demand beyond the standard pull-up through substantial asymmetrical loading.
readinessRequirements: strong unassisted pull-up control and advanced asymmetric pulling technique
exercises.description: An advanced asymmetric vertical pulling movement in which one arm performs more of the pulling work while the other remains extended.
setup: Use a secure pull-up bar or equivalent vertical pulling setup.
Begin from a controlled hang with the arms extended and the body stable beneath the bar.
Establish a controlled asymmetric pulling position.
steps: Pull upward while shifting the body toward the primary working arm.
Keep the assisting arm substantially straighter as the working-side chin approaches bar height.
Lower back to the starting hang with control, then alternate sides as prescribed.
completionCriteria: The working-side chin reaches bar height while the assisting arm remains substantially straighter.
The body returns to the starting hang with control.

exercises.name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
setupRequirements: secure horizontal or pull-up bar setup capable of supporting the body
exercises.placementRationale: Extends the tuck front-lever pathway by lengthening the body position and increasing the leverage demand.
readinessRequirements: advanced pulling and body-tension skill readiness
exercises.description: An advanced horizontal pulling lever with a more extended body position than the standard tuck front lever.
setup: Use a secure horizontal bar or equivalent support capable of supporting the body.
Start from a controlled straight-arm hang.
Bring the knees toward the chest while extending the hips so the body approaches a longer tucked lever.
steps: Pull into the advanced tucked lever position with the body more extended than the standard tuck.
Maintain whole-body tension and controlled scapular position.
Hold for the prescribed duration, then return to the starting position with control.
keyCues: Avoid swinging or collapsing through the shoulders.
completionCriteria: The advanced tucked lever position is established with the body held close to horizontal.
The prescribed hold duration is completed without losing the lever position.

crabWalkRestored.note: Restored as the earlier canonical locomotion foundation preceding Crab Reach.

verticalPullFoundationBackfilled.note: Moved earlier so the VERTICAL_PULL family begins before the final progression tiers.

resolvedTaxonomy: Scapular Wall Slide is treated as MOBILITY rather than HORIZONTAL_PULL.
Reverse Nordic is treated as KNEE_EXTENSION_QUADRICEPS rather than SQUAT.
Assisted Skater Squat is aligned with Skater Squat under SQUAT.
Side-Lying Oblique Crunch is treated as TRUNK_LATERAL_FLEXION rather than TRUNK_ROTATION.
Bird Dog, Cross-Body Dead Bug, Plank Shoulder Reach, Plank Shoulder Tap, and Bear Shoulder Tap are treated as TRUNK_ANTI_ROTATION rather than TRUNK_ANTI_EXTENSION/TRUNK_ROTATION.
integrationNotes.prescriptionSeparation: Tempo, pauses, range adjustments, assistance level, and workload remain outside the permanent exercise catalog and belong to the later prescription layer.
integrationNotes.tier8Policy: No new Tier 8 exercises are authored; the full current exercise vocabulary is unlocked by Tier 7.
verticalPullPathway: Scapular Pull-Up (5A) → Assisted Pull-Up (6C) → Pull-Up (7B) → Archer Pull-Up (7C)

horizontalPullBridge.note: Adds a genuine horizontal-pulling strength bridge between prone scapular work and the front-lever progression.

integrationNotes.unilateralSquatTaxonomy: True unilateral squat patterns are classified under SQUAT; LUNGE_SINGLE_LEG is reserved for lunge/step patterns.
integrationNotes.tier1Policy: Tier 1 intentionally retains its broad exercise pool so early users have sufficient appropriate movement variety; usageClass controls frequency rather than reducing the vocabulary.

advancedSkills: Higher-tier exercises represent advanced capabilities rather than requirements for every player.
Unlocking an exercise adds it to the permanent library; it does not require that the player perform it immediately.
Later exercise definitions should separately document setup, technique, readiness, and safety considerations.
impactSkills: Jumps, bounds, pogo hops, and burpee-jump movements should be treated as technique-dependent capabilities rather than movements whose workload should be increased without limit.

finalAuditFixes: Removed all remaining hidden “authored” placeholders from exercise definitions.
Moved Tuck Jump to SQUAT Stage 4 (Explosive Squat), where its movement semantics match the stage.
acceptedDesignDecisions: Tier 1 remains intentionally broad; raw Tier 1 exercise count is not treated as a defect.
Usage class controls how often exercises should surface in workouts: CORE, VARIETY, SPECIALIST.
No exercise vocabulary is added in Tier 8; all current vocabulary is unlocked by Tier 7.
Movement-stage order is family-specific and does not need to increase monotonically with overall game tier.
Reverse Plank remains under HINGE_HIP_EXTENSION as the closest existing capability fit.
The HINGE_HIP_EXTENSION branch may terminate before the highest tiers because posterior-chain progression continues through POSTERIOR_CHAIN_KNEE_FLEXION.
KNEE_EXTENSION_QUADRICEPS and TRUNK_LATERAL_FLEXION may remain specialized families with limited exercise counts.
